text: And from him, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim, from Ali Bin Abu Ali Al Lahby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having sid: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High would be Giving from the Rewards to the servant based upon the good manners, just as He<sup>azwj</sup> would Give to the fighter in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> (waking up) in the morning and going upon it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:49
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى لَيُعْطِي الْعَبْدَ مِنَ الثَّوَابِ عَلَى حُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ كَمَا يُعْطِي الْمُجَاهِدَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يَغْدُو عَلَيْهِ وَ يَرُوحُ .
citation.translation: And from him, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim, from Ali Bin Abu Ali Al Lahby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having sid: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High would be Giving from the Rewards to the servant based upon the good manners, just as He<sup>azwj</sup> would Give to the fighter in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> (waking up) in the morning and going upon it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (171/ 8)

text: From him, from Abdullah Al Hajjal, from Abu Usman Al Qabousy, from the one who mentioned, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blessed and High has Lent to His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> enemies the manners from the mannerisms of His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> friends, so that His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> friends can live along with His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> enemies in their governments’. And in another report, ‘(He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said): ‘And had it not been for that, they would not have left a (single) friend of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, except that they would have killed him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:49
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى أَعَارَ أَعْدَاءَهُ أَخْلَاقاً مِنْ أَخْلَاقِ أَوْلِيَائِهِ لِيَعِيشَ أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ مَعَ أَعْدَائِهِ فِي دَوْلَاتِهِمْ . وَ فِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى وَ لَوْ لَا ذَلِكَ لَمَا تَرَكُوا وَلِيّاً لِلَّهِ إِلَّا قَتَلُوهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Abdullah Al Hajjal, from Abu Usman Al Qabousy, from the one who mentioned, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blessed and High has Lent to His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> enemies the manners from the mannerisms of His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> friends, so that His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> friends can live along with His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> enemies in their governments’. And in another report, ‘(He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said): ‘And had it not been for that, they would not have left a (single) friend of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, except that they would have killed him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول وآخره مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/172)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar, from Al A’ala Bin Kamil who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When you mingle with the people, so if you have the capacity that you would not mingle with anyone from the people except that your hand would be higher upon his, then do so. So if the servant happens to have in him part of the deficiency from the worship, and there happens to be good manners for him, then Allahazwj would Make him to reach, due to his good manners, the level of the Fasting one, the standing one (for Salāt)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:49
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا خَالَطْتَ النَّاسَ فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ لَا تُخَالِطَ أَحَداً مِنَ النَّاسِ إِلَّا كَانَتْ يَدُكَ الْعُلْيَا عَلَيْهِ فَافْعَلْ فَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ يَكُونُ فِيهِ بَعْضُ التَّقْصِيرِ مِنَ الْعِبَادَةِ وَ يَكُونُ لَهُ حُسْنُ خُلُقٍ فَيُبَلِّغُهُ اللَّهُ بِ [حُسْنِ] خُلُقِهِ دَرَجَةَ الصَّائِمِ الْقَائِمِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar, from Al A’ala Bin Kamil who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When you mingle with the people, so if you have the capacity that you would not mingle with anyone from the people except that your hand would be higher upon his, then do so. So if the servant happens to have in him part of the deficiency from the worship, and there happens to be good manners for him, then Allahazwj would Make him to reach, due to his good manners, the level of the Fasting one, the standing one (for Salāt)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (172/ 8)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz Bin Abdullah, from Bahr Al Saqqa who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Bahr! Good manners are an affluence’. Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> inform you with a Hadeeth which is not in the hands of anyone from the people of Al-Medina?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘One day, while Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> was seated in the Masjid when a slave girl of one of the Helpers came over, and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> was sitting upright. So she grabbed a side of his<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> clothes. So the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> stood up for her, but she did not say anything, and the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> did not say anything to her, to the extent that she did that three times. So the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> stood up for her during the fourth attempt, and she was behind him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, so she took an edge of his<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> cloth, then retracted. So the people said to her, ‘May Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Deal with you and Do (whatever He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> may)! You withheld Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> three times, neither did you say anything to him nor did he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> say anything to you. What was your need to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>?’ She said, ‘For us there is a sick one. So my people sent me to take an edge from his<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> cloth in order to heal him by it. So whenever I wanted to take it, he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> saw me, and stood up. So I was too embarrased from him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> to take it while he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> sees me, and I disliked to demand him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> with regards to taking it, therefore I took it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:49
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَا بَحْرُ حُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ يُسْرٌ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَ لَا أُخْبِرُكَ بِحَدِيثٍ مَا هُوَ فِي يَدَيْ أَحَدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ قُلْتُ بَلَى قَالَ بَيْنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ جَالِسٌ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ إِذْ جَاءَتْ جَارِيَةٌ لِبَعْضِ الْأَنْصَارِ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ فَأَخَذَتْ بِطَرَفِ ثَوْبِهِ فَقَامَ لَهَا النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَلَمْ تَقُلْ شَيْئاً وَ لَمْ يَقُلْ لَهَا النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) شَيْئاً حَتَّى فَعَلَتْ ذَلِكَ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ فَقَامَ لَهَا النَّبِيُّ فِي الرَّابِعَةِ وَ هِيَ خَلْفَهُ فَأَخَذَتْ هُدْبَةً مِنْ ثَوْبِهِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَتْ فَقَالَ لَهَا النَّاسُ فَعَلَ اللَّهُ بِكِ وَ فَعَلَ حَبَسْتِ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ لَا تَقُولِينَ لَهُ شَيْئاً وَ لَا هُوَ يَقُولُ لَكِ شَيْئاً مَا كَانَتْ حَاجَتُكِ إِلَيْهِ قَالَتْ إِنَّ لَنَا مَرِيضاً فَأَرْسَلَنِي أَهْلِي لآِخُذَ هُدْبَةً مِنْ ثَوْبِهِ لِيَسْتَشْفِيَ بِهَا فَلَمَّا أَرَدْتُ أَخْذَهَا رَآنِي فَقَامَ فَاسْتَحْيَيْتُ مِنْهُ أَنْ آخُذَهَا وَ هُوَ يَرَانِي وَ أَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَسْتَأْمِرَهُ فِي أَخْذِهَا فَأَخَذْتُهَا .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Habeeb Al Khash’amy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The most preferable ones of you is the one of the best manners as his greatest quality, the one who is getting acquainted (with others), and they are getting acquainted with him modestly in their travels’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:49
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَفَاضِلُكُمْ أَحْسَنُكُمْ أَخْلَاقاً الْمُوَطَّئُونَ أَكْنَافاً الَّذِينَ يَأْلَفُونَ وَ يُؤْلَفُونَ وَ تُوَطَّأُ رِحَالُهُمْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Habeeb Al Khash’amy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The most preferable ones of you is the one of the best manners as his greatest quality, the one who is getting acquainted (with others), and they are getting acquainted with him modestly in their travels’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/174)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Maymoun Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘ A ‘Momin’ (the Believer) gets acquainted (with others), and there is no good in the one who neither gets acquainted nor does he get acquainted with’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:49
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) الْمُؤْمِنُ مَأْلُوفٌ وَ لَا خَيْرَ فِيمَنْ لَا يَأْلَفُ وَ لَا يُؤْلَفُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Maymoun Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘ A ‘Momin’ (the Believer) gets acquainted (with others), and there is no good in the one who neither gets acquainted nor does he get acquainted with’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (175/ 8)

text: Al Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The good manners makes its owner to reach the level of the Fasting one, the standing one (in Salāt)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:49
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ حُسْنَ الْخُلُقِ يَبْلُغُ بِصَاحِبِهِ دَرَجَةَ الصَّائِمِ الْقَائِمِ .
citation.translation: Al Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The good manners makes its owner to reach the level of the Fasting one, the standing one (in Salāt)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/175)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O sons of Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup>! You will never be equal to the people in their wealth, therefore meet them with the relaxed face and goodly cheerfulness’. And it is reported from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, (same as above) except that he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:50
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَا بَنِي عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ إِنَّكُمْ لَنْ تَسَعُوا النَّاسَ بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ فَالْقَوْهُمْ بِطَلَاقَةِ الْوَجْهِ وَ حُسْنِ الْبِشْرِ . وَ رَوَاهُ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ جَدِّهِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِلَّا أَنَّهُ قَالَ يَا بَنِي هَاشِمٍ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O sons of Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup>! You will never be equal to the people in their wealth, therefore meet them with the relaxed face and goodly cheerfulness’. And it is reported from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, (same as above) except that he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/176)

text: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (things), the one who goes to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with one of these, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Obligate the Paradise for him – the spending from poverty, and the cheerfulness to the entirety of the world, and the justice from himself’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:50
citation.arabic_text: ثَلَاثٌ مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِوَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ أَوْجَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ الْجَنَّةَ الْإِنْفَاقُ مِنْ إِقْتَارٍ وَ الْبِشْرُ لِجَمِيعِ الْعَالَمِ وَ الْإِنْصَافُ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (things), the one who goes to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with one of these, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Obligate the Paradise for him – the spending from poverty, and the cheerfulness to the entirety of the world, and the justice from himself’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/177)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboubn, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘A man came over to Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, so he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>! Advise me’. So, among what he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> advised him was that he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘Meet your brother with a cheerful face’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:50
citation.arabic_text: أَتَى رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَوْصِنِي فَكَانَ فِيمَا أَوْصَاهُ أَنْ قَالَ الْقَ أَخَاكَ بِوَجْهٍ مُنْبَسِطٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboubn, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘A man came over to Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, so he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>! Advise me’. So, among what he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> advised him was that he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘Meet your brother with a cheerful face’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (178/ 8)

text: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘What is the limit of the good manners?’ Heasws said: ‘Relax your arms, and be good in your speech, and meet your brother with goodly cheerfulness’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:50
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَا حَدُّ حُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ قَالَ تُلِينُ جَنَاحَكَ وَ تُطِيبُ كَلَامَكَ وَ تَلْقَى أَخَاكَ بِبِشْرٍ حَسَنٍ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘What is the limit of the good manners?’ Heasws said: ‘Relax your arms, and be good in your speech, and meet your brother with goodly cheerfulness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل كالحسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/178)

text: From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Fuzayl who said, ‘The good works and the goodly cheerfulness both amass the love and cause to enter the Paradise; and the stinginess and a frown face both cause remoteness from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and cause to enter the Fire’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:50
citation.arabic_text: صَنَائِعُ الْمَعْرُوفِ وَ حُسْنُ الْبِشْرِ يَكْسِبَانِ الْمَحَبَّةَ وَ يُدْخِلَانِ الْجَنَّةَ وَ الْبُخْلُ وَ عُبُوسُ الْوَجْهِ يُبْعِدَانِ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَ يُدْخِلَانِ النَّارَ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Fuzayl who said, ‘The good works and the goodly cheerfulness both amass the love and cause to enter the Paradise; and the stinginess and a frown face both cause remoteness from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and cause to enter the Fire’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: كالصحيح موقو ف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/179)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The goodly cheerfulness does away with the grudges’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:50
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) حُسْنُ الْبِشْرِ يَذْهَبُ بِالسَّخِيمَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The goodly cheerfulness does away with the grudges’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/180)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not Send a Prophet except with truthful narrations, and repayment of the entrustments to the righteous as well as the immoral’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لَمْ يَبْعَثْ نَبِيّاً إِلَّا بِصِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ وَ أَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ إِلَى الْبَرِّ وَ الْفَاجِرِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not Send a Prophet except with truthful narrations, and repayment of the entrustments to the righteous as well as the immoral’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (180/ 8)

text: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq bin Ammar, and someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Do not be deceived by their Salāt and by their Fasting, for sometimes the man gets habitual with the Salāt and the Fasting to the extent that if he were to leave it, he gets terrified. But, get their information during the truthful narration and the repayment of the entrustments’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: لَا تَغْتَرُّوا بِصَلَاتِهِمْ وَ لَا بِصِيَامِهِمْ فَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ رُبَّمَا لَهِجَ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَ الصَّوْمِ حَتَّى لَوْ تَرَكَهُ اسْتَوْحَشَ وَ لَكِنِ اخْتَبِرُوهُمْ عِنْدَ صِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ وَ أَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq bin Ammar, and someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Do not be deceived by their Salāt and by their Fasting, for sometimes the man gets habitual with the Salāt and the Fasting to the extent that if he were to leave it, he gets terrified. But, get their information during the truthful narration and the repayment of the entrustments’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/181)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Musna Al Hannat, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who is truthful of his tongue would purify his deed’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ صَدَقَ لِسَانُهُ زَكَى عَمَلُهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Musna Al Hannat, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who is truthful of his tongue would purify his deed’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/181)

text: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Musa Bin Sa’dan, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘With regards to the first thing you indulge in is to learn the truthfulness before (discussing) the Hadeeth’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فِي أَوَّلِ دَخْلَةٍ دَخَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ تَعَلَّمُوا الصِّدْقَ قَبْلَ الْحَدِيثِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Musa Bin Sa’dan, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘With regards to the first thing you indulge in is to learn the truthfulness before (discussing) the Hadeeth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/182)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Kahmasy who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour conveys the greetings to you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And upon him be the greetings. When you go to Abdullah, so convey the greetings and say to him that Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> is saying to you: ‘Look at what Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> reached with in the presence of Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, so necessitate it, for Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, rather, reached whatever he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> reached with in the presence of Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> by truthful narrations and repayment of the entrustments’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ يُقْرِئُكَ السَّلَامَ قَالَ عَلَيْكَ وَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ إِذَا أَتَيْتَ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ فَأَقْرِئْهُ السَّلَامَ وَ قُلْ لَهُ إِنَّ جَعْفَرَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ يَقُولُ لَكَ انْظُرْ مَا بَلَغَ بِهِ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَالْزَمْهُ فَإِنَّ عَلِيّاً ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّمَا بَلَغَ مَا بَلَغَ بِهِ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بِصِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ وَ أَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Kahmasy who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour conveys the greetings to you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And upon him be the greetings. When you go to Abdullah, so convey the greetings and say to him that Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> is saying to you: ‘Look at what Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> reached with in the presence of Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, so necessitate it, for Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, rather, reached whatever he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> reached with in the presence of Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> by truthful narrations and repayment of the entrustments’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (183/ 8)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ismail Al Basry, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘O Fuzayl! The truthful is the first one whom Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Ratifies. He knows that he is truthful, and its ratification is that he comes to know that he is truthful’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَا فُضَيْلُ إِنَّ الصَّادِقَ أَوَّلُ مَنْ يُصَدِّقُهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ صَادِقٌ وَ تُصَدِّقُهُ نَفْسُهُ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ صَادِقٌ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ismail Al Basry, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘O Fuzayl! The truthful is the first one whom Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Ratifies. He knows that he is truthful, and its ratification is that he comes to know that he is truthful’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/183)

text: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Hazim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘But rather Ismail<sup>as</sup> was named as ‘truthful of the promise’ because he<sup>as</sup> promised a man (to be) in a particular place, so he<sup>asws</sup> waited for him in that place for a year. Therefore Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Named him<sup>as</sup> as ‘The truthful of the promise’’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man did come to him<sup>as</sup> after that, so Ismail<sup>as</sup> said to him: ‘I<sup>as</sup> did not cease waiting for you’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّمَا سُمِّيَ إِسْمَاعِيلُ صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ لِأَنَّهُ وَعَدَ رَجُلًا فِي مَكَانٍ فَانْتَظَرَهُ فِي ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ سَنَةً فَسَمَّاهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ ثُمَّ قَالَ إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ أَتَاهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ لَهُ إِسْمَاعِيلُ مَا زِلْتُ مُنْتَظِراً لَكَ .
citation.translation: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Hazim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘But rather Ismail<sup>as</sup> was named as ‘truthful of the promise’ because he<sup>as</sup> promised a man (to be) in a particular place, so he<sup>asws</sup> waited for him in that place for a year. Therefore Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Named him<sup>as</sup> as ‘The truthful of the promise’’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man did come to him<sup>as</sup> after that, so Ismail<sup>as</sup> said to him: ‘I<sup>as</sup> did not cease waiting for you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/184)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar Al Khazzaz, from his grandfather Al Rabie Bin Sa’ad who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Rabie! Let the man be truthful until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Writes him as a truthful one’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) يَا رَبِيعُ إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَصْدُقُ حَتَّى يَكْتُبَهُ اللَّهُ صِدِّيقاً .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar Al Khazzaz, from his grandfather Al Rabie Bin Sa’ad who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Rabie! Let the man be truthful until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Writes him as a truthful one’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (184/ 8)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The servant, could be truthful until he is Written in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> as being from the truthful ones, and he could lie until he is Written in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> as being from the liars. So when he is truthful, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Says: “He is truthful and righteous”; and when he lies, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Says: “Liar, and an immoral one”’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِنَّ الْعَبْدَ لَيَصْدُقُ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ وَ يَكْذِبُ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ فَإِذَا صَدَقَ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ صَدَقَ وَ بَرَّ وَ إِذَا كَذَبَ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ كَذَبَ وَ فَجَرَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The servant, could be truthful until he is Written in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> as being from the truthful ones, and he could lie until he is Written in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> as being from the liars. So when he is truthful, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Says: “He is truthful and righteous”; and when he lies, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Says: “Liar, and an immoral one”’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (185/ 8)

text: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘(You should) be inspiring people with the goodness without using tongues (calling them). Let them see from you the striving, and the truthfulness, and the piety’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: كُونُوا دُعَاةً لِلنَّاسِ بِالْخَيْرِ بِغَيْرِ أَلْسِنَتِكُمْ لِيَرَوْا مِنْكُمُ الِاجْتِهَادَ وَ الصِّدْقَ وَ الْوَرَعَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘(You should) be inspiring people with the goodness without using tongues (calling them). Let them see from you the striving, and the truthfulness, and the piety’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/186)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam who said, ‘Abu Al Waleed Hassan Bin Ziyad Al Sayqal said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who is truthful of his tongue would purify his deed, and the one who is good of intention would increase in his livelihood, and the one of goodly righteousness with his family members, there would be an extension for him in his life-span’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو الْوَلِيدِ حَسَنُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ الصَّيْقَلُ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَنْ صَدَقَ لِسَانُهُ زَكَى عَمَلُهُ وَ مَنْ حَسُنَتْ نِيَّتُهُ زِيدَ فِي رِزْقِهِ وَ مَنْ حَسُنَ بِرُّهُ بِأَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ مُدَّ لَهُ فِي عُمُرِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam who said, ‘Abu Al Waleed Hassan Bin Ziyad Al Sayqal said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who is truthful of his tongue would purify his deed, and the one who is good of intention would increase in his livelihood, and the one of goodly righteousness with his family members, there would be an extension for him in his life-span’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (186/ 8)

text: From him, from Abu Talib, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not be looking at the prolonged Bowing and Prostration of the man, for in that is something of his habit, were he to leave it, he would be petrified due to that. But look at the truthfulness of his narration and the repayment of his entrustment’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:51
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَنْظُرُوا إِلَى طُولِ رُكُوعِ الرَّجُلِ وَ سُجُودِهِ فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ شَيْ‏ءٌ اعْتَادَهُ فَلَوْ تَرَكَهُ اسْتَوْحَشَ لِذَلِكَ وَ لَكِنِ انْظُرُوا إِلَى صِدْقِ حَدِيثِهِ وَ أَدَاءِ أَمَانَتِهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Abu Talib, raising it, said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not be looking at the prolonged Bowing and Prostration of the man, for in that is something of his habit, were he to leave it, he would be petrified due to that. But look at the truthfulness of his narration and the repayment of his entrustment’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/186)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Abu Umeyda Al Haza’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Hiyā’ the bashfulness is from the Emān, and the Emān is in the Paradise’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:52
citation.arabic_text: الْحَيَاءُ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ وَ الْإِيمَانُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Abu Umeyda Al Haza’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Hiyā’ the bashfulness is from the Emān, and the Emān is in the Paradise’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/187)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Sayqal who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The Hiyā, and the chastity, and the tiredness, meaning the tiredness of the tongue not tiredness of the heart, is from the Emān’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:52
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْحَيَاءُ وَ الْعَفَافُ وَ الْعِيُّ أَعْنِي عِيَّ اللِّسَانِ لَا عِيَّ الْقَلْبِ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Sayqal who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The Hiyā, and the chastity, and the tiredness, meaning the tiredness of the tongue not tiredness of the heart, is from the Emān’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/188)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Mus’ab Bin Yazeed, from Al Awwan Bin al Zubeyr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who softens his face would soften his knowledge’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:52
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ رَقَّ وَجْهُهُ رَقَّ عِلْمُهُ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Mus’ab Bin Yazeed, from Al Awwan Bin al Zubeyr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who softens his face would soften his knowledge’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/188)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Yahya a brother of Darim, from Muaz Bin Kaseer, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) having said: ‘Hiyā and the Emān are paired in one coupling, so when one of the two goes, its counterpart follows it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:52
citation.arabic_text: الْحَيَاءُ وَ الْإِيمَانُ مَقْرُونَانِ فِي قَرَنٍ فَإِذَا ذَهَبَ أَحَدُهُمَا تَبِعَهُ صَاحِبُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Yahya a brother of Darim, from Muaz Bin Kaseer, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) having said: ‘Hiyā and the Emān are paired in one coupling, so when one of the two goes, its counterpart follows it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/189)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Al Fazl Bin Kaseer, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘There is no Emān for the one who has no ‘Hiyā’ bashfulness for him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:52
citation.arabic_text: لَا إِيمَانَ لِمَنْ لَا حَيَاءَ لَهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Al Fazl Bin Kaseer, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘There is no Emān for the one who has no ‘Hiyā’ bashfulness for him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/190)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of our companions, raising it, ‘Heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The Hiyā (bashfulness) is of two (types) – The Hiyā of the intellect and the Hiyā of foolishness. So the Hiyā of the intellect, it is the knowledge, and the Hiyā of the foolishness, it is the ignorance’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:52
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) الْحَيَاءُ حَيَاءَانِ حَيَاءُ عَقْلٍ وَ حَيَاءُ حُمْقٍ فَحَيَاءُ الْعَقْلِ هُوَ الْعِلْمُ وَ حَيَاءُ الْحُمْقِ هُوَ الْجَهْلُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of our companions, raising it, ‘Heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The Hiyā (bashfulness) is of two (types) – The Hiyā of the intellect and the Hiyā of foolishness. So the Hiyā of the intellect, it is the knowledge, and the Hiyā of the foolishness, it is the ignorance’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (190/ 8)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim, from Ali Bin Abu Ali Al Lahby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Four (things), the one who has these in him, and (even if) he was (immersed) in sins from his head to his toe, Allahazwj would Change these to good deeds – The truthfulness, and the Hiyā (bashfulness), and the good manners, and the gratefulness’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:52
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَرْبَعٌ مَنْ كُنَّ فِيهِ وَ كَانَ مِنْ قَرْنِهِ إِلَى قَدَمِهِ ذُنُوباً بَدَّلَهَا اللَّهُ حَسَنَاتٍ الصِّدْقُ وَ الْحَيَاءُ وَ حُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ وَ الشُّكْرُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim, from Ali Bin Abu Ali Al Lahby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Four (things), the one who has these in him, and (even if) he was (immersed) in sins from his head to his toe, Allahazwj would Change these to good deeds – The truthfulness, and the Hiyā (bashfulness), and the good manners, and the gratefulness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/190)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said in his<sup>saww</sup> sermon: ‘Shall I<sup>saww</sup> inform you with the best moral of the world and the Hereafter? (it is) the pardoning the one who oppressed you, and maintaining relations with the one who cut you off, and the (doing of) favours to the one who offended you, and giving to the one who deprived you’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:53
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فِي خُطْبَتِهِ أَ لَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِخَيْرِ خَلَائِقِ الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ الْعَفْوُ عَمَّنْ ظَلَمَكَ وَ تَصِلُ مَنْ قَطَعَكَ وَ الْإِحْسَانُ إِلَى مَنْ أَسَاءَ إِلَيْكَ وَ إِعْطَاءُ مَنْ حَرَمَكَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said in his<sup>saww</sup> sermon: ‘Shall I<sup>saww</sup> inform you with the best moral of the world and the Hereafter? (it is) the pardoning the one who oppressed you, and maintaining relations with the one who cut you off, and the (doing of) favours to the one who offended you, and giving to the one who deprived you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (192/ 8)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Gurrat Bin Dinar Al Raqqy, from Abu Is’haq Al Sabi’e who said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>saww</sup> point you to the best of the manners of the world and the Hereafter? (It is) maintaining relations with the one who cut you off, and giving to the one who deprives you, and pardoning the one who oppresses you’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:53
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَ لَا أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى خَيْرِ أَخْلَاقِ الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ تَصِلُ مَنْ قَطَعَكَ وَ تُعْطِي مَنْ حَرَمَكَ وَ تَعْفُو عَمَّنْ ظَلَمَكَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Gurrat Bin Dinar Al Raqqy, from Abu Is’haq Al Sabi’e who said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>saww</sup> point you to the best of the manners of the world and the Hereafter? (It is) maintaining relations with the one who cut you off, and giving to the one who deprives you, and pardoning the one who oppresses you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/192)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Abu Abdullah Shuayb Al Faify, from Humran Bin Ayn who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three are from the nobilities of the world and the Hereafter – your pardoning the one who oppresses you, and your maintain relations with the one who cuts you off, and your forbearing when you are being ignored upon’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:53
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) ثَلَاثٌ مِنْ مَكَارِمِ الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ تَعْفُو عَمَّنْ ظَلَمَكَ وَ تَصِلُ مَنْ قَطَعَكَ وَ تَحْلُمُ إِذَا جُهِلَ عَلَيْكَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Abu Abdullah Shuayb Al Faify, from Humran Bin Ayn who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three are from the nobilities of the world and the Hereafter – your pardoning the one who oppresses you, and your maintain relations with the one who cuts you off, and your forbearing when you are being ignored upon’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/193)

text: Ali, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When it will be the Day of Judgement, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High will Gather the former ones and the later ones in one plain. Then a Caller will Call out: ‘Where are the people of merit?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So some necks from the people would be standing, and the Angels would meet them and saying to them: ‘And what was your merit?’ So they would be saying, ‘We used to maintain relations with the ones who cut us off, and we gave to the ones who deprived us, and we pardoned the ones who oppressed us’. So it would be said to them: ‘You are speaking the truth. Enter into the Paradise!’’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:53
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ إِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ جَمَعَ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى الْأَوَّلِينَ وَ الْآخِرِينَ فِي صَعِيدٍ وَاحِدٍ ثُمَّ يُنَادِي مُنَادٍ أَيْنَ أَهْلُ الْفَضْلِ قَالَ فَيَقُومُ عُنُقٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ فَتَلَقَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ فَيَقُولُونَ وَ مَا كَانَ فَضْلُكُمْ فَيَقُولُونَ كُنَّا نَصِلُ مَنْ قَطَعَنَا وَ نُعْطِي مَنْ حَرَمَنَا وَ نَعْفُو عَمَّنْ ظَلَمَنَا قَالَ فَيُقَالُ لَهُمْ صَدَقْتُمُ ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ .
citation.translation: Ali, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When it will be the Day of Judgement, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High will Gather the former ones and the later ones in one plain. Then a Caller will Call out: ‘Where are the people of merit?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So some necks from the people would be standing, and the Angels would meet them and saying to them: ‘And what was your merit?’ So they would be saying, ‘We used to maintain relations with the ones who cut us off, and we gave to the ones who deprived us, and we pardoned the ones who oppressed us’. So it would be said to them: ‘You are speaking the truth. Enter into the Paradise!’’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/193)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Jahm Bin Al Hakam Al Madainy, from Ismail Bin Abu Ziyad Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated)from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is upon you with the pardoning, for the pardoning does not increase the servant (with anything) except for honour, therefore pardon, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will Honour you’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:53
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْعَفْوِ فَإِنَّ الْعَفْوَ لَا يَزِيدُ الْعَبْدَ إِلَّا عِزّاً فَتَعَافَوْا يُعِزَّكُمُ اللَّهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Jahm Bin Al Hakam Al Madainy, from Ismail Bin Abu Ziyad Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated)from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is upon you with the pardoning, for the pardoning does not increase the servant (with anything) except for honour, therefore pardon, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will Honour you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (194/ 8)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Khalid Al Qammat, from Humran, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The regret upon the pardoning is superior and easier than the regret upon the punishing’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:53
citation.arabic_text: النَّدَامَةُ عَلَى الْعَفْوِ أَفْضَلُ وَ أَيْسَرُ مِنَ النَّدَامَةِ عَلَى الْعُقُوبَةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Khalid Al Qammat, from Humran, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The regret upon the pardoning is superior and easier than the regret upon the punishing’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور حسن عند ي - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/194)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Sa’dan, from Mo’tab who said, ‘It was so that Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> was by a (garden) wall of his<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> looked at a slave of his<sup>asws</sup> who had taken a bunch of dates, and he threw it behind the wall. So I went over to him, and seized it and went with him to him<sup>asws</sup>, and I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I found this one that this bunch (of dates)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to the slave: ‘O so and so!’ He said, ‘At your<sup>asws</sup> service!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Are you hungry?’ He said, ‘Yes, my Master<sup>asws</sup>!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So are you bare (need clothes)?’ He said, ‘Yes, my Master<sup>asws</sup>!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So, for which thing (reason) did you take these?’ He said, ‘I desired that’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Go, for these are for you’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Leave him alone’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:53
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى ( عليه السلام ) فِي حَائِطٍ لَهُ يَصْرِمُ فَنَظَرْتُ إِلَى غُلَامٍ لَهُ قَدْ أَخَذَ كَارَةً مِنْ تَمْرٍ فَرَمَى بِهَا وَرَاءَ الْحَائِطِ فَأَتَيْتُهُ وَ أَخَذْتُهُ وَ ذَهَبْتُ بِهِ إِلَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنِّي وَجَدْتُ هَذَا وَ هَذِهِ الْكَارَةَ فَقَالَ لِلْغُلَامِ يَا فُلَانُ قَالَ لَبَّيْكَ قَالَ أَ تَجُوعُ قَالَ لَا يَا سَيِّدِي قَالَ فَتَعْرَى قَالَ لَا يَا سَيِّدِي قَالَ فَلِأَيِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ أَخَذْتَ هَذِهِ قَالَ اشْتَهَيْتُ ذَلِكَ قَالَ اذْهَبْ فَهِيَ لَكَ وَ قَالَ خَلُّوا عَنْهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Sa’dan, from Mo’tab who said, ‘It was so that Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> was by a (garden) wall of his<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> looked at a slave of his<sup>asws</sup> who had taken a bunch of dates, and he threw it behind the wall. So I went over to him, and seized it and went with him to him<sup>asws</sup>, and I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I found this one that this bunch (of dates)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to the slave: ‘O so and so!’ He said, ‘At your<sup>asws</sup> service!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Are you hungry?’ He said, ‘Yes, my Master<sup>asws</sup>!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So are you bare (need clothes)?’ He said, ‘Yes, my Master<sup>asws</sup>!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So, for which thing (reason) did you take these?’ He said, ‘I desired that’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Go, for these are for you’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Leave him alone’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/195)

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘No two parties ever met (in a confrontation) at all, except victory was for the one who was greater of the two in pardoning’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:53
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَا الْتَقَتْ فِئَتَانِ قَطُّ إِلَّا نُصِرَ أَعْظَمُهُمَا عَفْواً .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘No two parties ever met (in a confrontation) at all, except victory was for the one who was greater of the two in pardoning’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (195/ 8)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘They came to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> with the Jewess who had poisoned the sheep for the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> said to her: ‘What carried you upon what you did?’ So she said, ‘I said, ‘If he<sup>saww</sup> is a Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, it would not harm him, and if he was a king, the people would be relieved from him<sup>saww</sup>’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> pardoned her from it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:53
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أُتِيَ بِالْيَهُودِيَّةِ الَّتِي سَمَّتِ الشَّاةَ لِلنَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقَالَ لَهَا مَا حَمَلَكِ عَلَى مَا صَنَعْتِ فَقَالَتْ قُلْتُ إِنْ كَانَ نَبِيّاً لَمْ يَضُرَّهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ مَلِكاً أَرَحْتُ النَّاسَ مِنْهُ قَالَ فَعَفَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَنْهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘They came to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> with the Jewess who had poisoned the sheep for the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> said to her: ‘What carried you upon what you did?’ So she said, ‘I said, ‘If he<sup>saww</sup> is a Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, it would not harm him, and if he was a king, the people would be relieved from him<sup>saww</sup>’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> pardoned her from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (196/ 8)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (actions), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Increase by these the personality of the Muslim except for honour – the pardoning of the one who oppressed him, and giving to the one who deprived him, and the maintaining of the relationship with the one who cuts off from him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:53
citation.arabic_text: ثَلَاثٌ لَا يَزِيدُ اللَّهُ بِهِنَّ الْمَرْءَ الْمُسْلِمَ إِلَّا عِزّاً الصَّفْحُ عَمَّنْ ظَلَمَهُ وَ إِعْطَاءُ مَنْ حَرَمَهُ وَ الصِّلَةُ لِمَنْ قَطَعَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (actions), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Increase by these the personality of the Muslim except for honour – the pardoning of the one who oppressed him, and giving to the one who deprived him, and the maintaining of the relationship with the one who cuts off from him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (196/ 8)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not love to humiliate myself<sup>asws</sup> for the Bounties, and I<sup>asws</sup> have not swallowed a portion more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than the portion of anger, not seeking retribution by it from its agitator’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:54
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَا أُحِبُّ أَنَّ لِي بِذُلِّ نَفْسِي حُمْرَ النَّعَمِ وَ مَا تَجَرَّعْتُ جُرْعَةً أَحَبَّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ جُرْعَةِ غَيْظٍ لَا أُكَافِي بِهَا صَاحِبَهَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not love to humiliate myself<sup>asws</sup> for the Bounties, and I<sup>asws</sup> have not swallowed a portion more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than the portion of anger, not seeking retribution by it from its agitator’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (197/ 8)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, and Ali Bin al uman, from Ammar Bin Marwan, from Zayd Al Shahaam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The best swallowing of the anger is for the one who is patient upon it, for the great Recompense is for the one (subjected to) great afflictions, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Love a people except He<sup>azwj</sup> Tests them’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:54
citation.arabic_text: نِعْمَ الْجُرْعَةُ الْغَيْظُ لِمَنْ صَبَرَ عَلَيْهَا فَإِنَّ عَظِيمَ الْأَجْرِ لَمِنْ عَظِيمِ الْبَلَاءِ وَ مَا أَحَبَّ اللَّهُ قَوْماً إِلَّا ابْتَلَاهُمْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, and Ali Bin al uman, from Ammar Bin Marwan, from Zayd Al Shahaam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The best swallowing of the anger is for the one who is patient upon it, for the great Recompense is for the one (subjected to) great afflictions, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Love a people except He<sup>azwj</sup> Tests them’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/198)

text: From him, from Ali Bin Al Numan and Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ammar Bin Marwan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said: ‘Observe patience upon the enemies of the Favours, for you will never be sufficed from the one who disobeys Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding you by anything more superior than obeying Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding him (by being patient)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:54
citation.arabic_text: اصْبِرْ عَلَى أَعْدَاءِ النِّعَمِ فَإِنَّكَ لَنْ تُكَافِئَ مَنْ عَصَى اللَّهَ فِيكَ بِأَفْضَلَ مِنْ أَنْ تُطِيعَ اللَّهَ فِيهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ali Bin Al Numan and Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ammar Bin Marwan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said: ‘Observe patience upon the enemies of the Favours, for you will never be sufficed from the one who disobeys Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding you by anything more superior than obeying Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding him (by being patient)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (199/ 8)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Sabit, a slave of the family of Hareyz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Supressing the anger from the enemies in their government by dissimulation is prudence for the one who takes by it, and is a protection from the exposure to the affliction in the world and the animosity of the enemies in their government, and opposition to them in their government without dissimulation is to neglect the Command of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. Therefore, pay compliments to the people, that would nourish for you in their presence, and do not make enemies out of them, so they would be riding upon your necks and humiliate you’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:54
citation.arabic_text: كَظْمُ الْغَيْظِ عَنِ الْعَدُوِّ فِي دَوْلَاتِهِمْ تَقِيَّةً حَزْمٌ لِمَنْ أَخَذَ بِهِ وَ تَحَرُّزٌ مِنَ التَّعَرُّضِ لِلْبَلَاءِ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَ مُعَانَدَةُ الْأَعْدَاءِ فِي دَوْلَاتِهِمْ وَ مُمَاظَّتُهُمْ فِي غَيْرِ تَقِيَّةٍ تَرْكُ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ فَجَامِلُوا النَّاسَ يَسْمَنْ ذَلِكَ لَكُمْ عِنْدَهُمْ وَ لَا تُعَادُوهُمْ فَتَحْمِلُوهُمْ عَلَى رِقَابِكُمْ فَتَذِلُّوا .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Sabit, a slave of the family of Hareyz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Supressing the anger from the enemies in their government by dissimulation is prudence for the one who takes by it, and is a protection from the exposure to the affliction in the world and the animosity of the enemies in their government, and opposition to them in their government without dissimulation is to neglect the Command of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. Therefore, pay compliments to the people, that would nourish for you in their presence, and do not make enemies out of them, so they would be riding upon your necks and humiliate you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/199)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from one of his companions, from Malik Bin Husayn Al Sakuny who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘There is none form a servant who suppresses anger except that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Increases him with honour in the world and the Hereafter; and Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said [3:134] and those who restrain (their) anger and pardon the people; and Allah Loves the doers of good (to others), and Allahazwj would Reward him in place of that anger’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:54
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا مِنْ عَبْدٍ كَظَمَ غَيْظاً إِلَّا زَادَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عِزّاً فِي الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ وَ قَدْ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ الْكاظِمِينَ الْغَيْظَ وَ الْعافِينَ عَنِ النَّاسِ وَ اللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ وَ أَثَابَهُ اللَّهُ مَكَانَ غَيْظِهِ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from one of his companions, from Malik Bin Husayn Al Sakuny who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘There is none form a servant who suppresses anger except that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Increases him with honour in the world and the Hereafter; and Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said [3:134] and those who restrain (their) anger and pardon the people; and Allah Loves the doers of good (to others), and Allahazwj would Reward him in place of that anger’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/200)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Sayf Bin Ameyra who said, ‘It was narrated to me by the one who heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who suppresses anger, and (even though) had he so desired to he could have continued it (his anger), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Fill his heart on the Day of Judgement with His<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:54
citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي مَنْ سَمِعَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَنْ كَظَمَ غَيْظاً وَ لَوْ شَاءَ أَنْ يُمْضِيَهُ أَمْضَاهُ أَمْلَأَ اللَّهُ قَلْبَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ رِضَاهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Sayf Bin Ameyra who said, ‘It was narrated to me by the one who heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who suppresses anger, and (even though) had he so desired to he could have continued it (his anger), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Fill his heart on the Day of Judgement with His<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/201)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Munzir, from Al Wassafy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘The one who suppresses anger and he is able upon continuing it, Allahazwj would Fill his heart with security and Emān on the Day of Judgement’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:54
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ كَظَمَ غَيْظاً وَ هُوَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى إِمْضَائِهِ حَشَا اللَّهُ قَلْبَهُ أَمْناً وَ إِيمَاناً يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Munzir, from Al Wassafy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘The one who suppresses anger and he is able upon continuing it, Allahazwj would Fill his heart with security and Emān on the Day of Judgement’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/202)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Abdul Kareem Bin Amro, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shahham, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said to me: ‘O Zayd! Observe patience upon the enemies of the favours, for you will never suffice yourself from the one who disobeys Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding you with anything more superior than your obedience to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding him. O Zayd! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Chose Al-Islam and Selected it, therefore be good companions of it by the generosity and the best manners’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:54
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي يَا زَيْدُ اصْبِرْ عَلَى أَعْدَاءِ النِّعَمِ فَإِنَّكَ لَنْ تُكَافِئَ مَنْ عَصَى اللَّهَ فِيكَ بِأَفْضَلَ مِنْ أَنْ تُطِيعَ اللَّهَ فِيهِ يَا زَيْدُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَى الْإِسْلَامَ وَ اخْتَارَهُ فَأَحْسِنُوا صُحْبَتَهُ بِالسَّخَاءِ وَ حُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Abdul Kareem Bin Amro, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shahham, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said to me: ‘O Zayd! Observe patience upon the enemies of the favours, for you will never suffice yourself from the one who disobeys Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding you with anything more superior than your obedience to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding him. O Zayd! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Chose Al-Islam and Selected it, therefore be good companions of it by the generosity and the best manners’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (202/ 8)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Hafs Baya’a Al Sabiry, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who loves the Way to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic should swallow two portions – the potion of anger repelling it by the forbearance, and a portion of difficulties repelling it with patience’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:54
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مِنْ أَحَبِّ السَّبِيلِ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ جُرْعَتَانِ جُرْعَةُ غَيْظٍ تَرُدُّهَا بِحِلْمٍ وَ جُرْعَةُ مُصِيبَةٍ تَرُدُّهَا بِصَبْرٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Hafs Baya’a Al Sabiry, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who loves the Way to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic should swallow two portions – the potion of anger repelling it by the forbearance, and a portion of difficulties repelling it with patience’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/202)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from the one who narrated it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said to me: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>! There is none from the things more delighting to the eyes of your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> than swallowing the potion of anger, its consequence being patience, and there is none from the most noble of the bounties which would bring me any happiness if it may cause humiliation to my soul’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:54
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبِي يَا بُنَيَّ مَا مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ أَقَرَّ لِعَيْنِ أَبِيكَ مِنْ جُرْعَةِ غَيْظٍ عَاقِبَتُهَا صَبْرٌ وَ مَا مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ يَسُرُّنِي أَنَّ لِي بِذُلِّ نَفْسِي حُمْرَ النَّعَمِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from the one who narrated it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said to me: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>! There is none from the things more delighting to the eyes of your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> than swallowing the potion of anger, its consequence being patience, and there is none from the most noble of the bounties which would bring me any happiness if it may cause humiliation to my soul’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Muaz Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Observe patient upon the enemies of the favours, for you will never be sufficed from the one who disobeys Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding you by anything more superior than if you were to obey Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding him (by suppression of anger)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:54
citation.arabic_text: اصْبِرُوا عَلَى أَعْدَاءِ النِّعَمِ فَإِنَّكَ لَنْ تُكَافِئَ مَنْ عَصَى اللَّهَ فِيكَ بِأَفْضَلَ مِنْ أَنْ تُطِيعَ اللَّهَ فِيهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Muaz Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Observe patient upon the enemies of the favours, for you will never be sufficed from the one who disobeys Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding you by anything more superior than if you were to obey Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding him (by suppression of anger)’.
