text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Jameela who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Mominen<sup>asws</sup> wrote to one of his<sup>asws</sup> companions advising him: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> hereby advise you, and myself<sup>asws</sup> with fearing the One<sup>azwj</sup> the disobedience to Whom is not Permissible. Neither can anyone else be hoped to nor can anyone be self-sufficient except by Him<sup>azwj</sup>, for the one who fears Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Majestic and Mighty would be strong, and satiated and quenched, and his intellect would be higher than the people of the world. So his body would be with the people of the world but his heart and mind would be eyeing the Hereafter. Thus, he would extinguish by the illumination of his heart, whatever his eyes visualize from the love of the world. So he considers its Prohibitions as filthy and keeps aside from its doubtful matters, which would harm (him), by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, with the clear Permissible, except what is inevitable for him from its crumbs, intensifying his backbone with it, and a (piece of) cloth to cover his nakedness with from the most coarse of what he can find and its roughest. And there does not happen to be for him, regarding what is inevitable for him from it, neither any reliability nor hope. So his reliance and his hopes are upon the Creator of the things, therefore he struggles, and strives, and exhausts his body until his ribs are manifested and his two eyes sink. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Exchanges for him, from that, strength in his body, and intensity in his intellect, and whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> has Treasured for him in the Hereafter is more. Therefore, reject the world, for the love of the world would blind, and deaf and mute, and would disgrace the necks. So manage whatever is remaining from your life and do not say, ‘Tomorrow’, or ‘After tomorrow’, for rather, destroyed were the ones who were before you by their staying upon their aspirations and their procrastinations until the Command of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> came to them suddenly and they were oblivious. So they were transferred upon the planks (of wood) into their graves, the dark, the narrow, and the children and the family members had submitted them. So he was cut-off to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with a penitent heart from rejecting the world and a determination where was not breakage nor betrayal. May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Assist us<sup>asws</sup> and you upon obeying Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Harmonise us<sup>asws</sup> and you to His<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:61
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) كَتَبَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِلَى بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ يَعِظُهُ أُوصِيكَ وَ نَفْسِي بِتَقْوَى مَنْ لَا تَحِلُّ مَعْصِيَتُهُ وَ لَا يُرْجَى غَيْرُهُ وَ لَا الْغِنَى إِلَّا بِهِ فَإِنَّ مَنِ اتَّقَى اللَّهَ جَلَّ وَ عَزَّ وَ قَوِيَ وَ شَبِعَ وَ رَوِيَ وَ رُفِعَ عَقْلُهُ عَنْ أَهْلِ الدُّنْيَا فَبَدَنُهُ مَعَ أَهْلِ الدُّنْيَا وَ قَلْبُهُ وَ عَقْلُهُ مُعَايِنُ الْآخِرَةِ فَأَطْفَأَ بِضَوْءِ قَلْبِهِ مَا أَبْصَرَتْ عَيْنَاهُ مِنْ حُبِّ الدُّنْيَا فَقَذَّرَ حَرَامَهَا وَ جَانَبَ شُبُهَاتِهَا وَ أَضَرَّ وَ اللَّهِ بِالْحَلَالِ الصَّافِي إِلَّا مَا لَا بُدَّ لَهُ مِنْ كِسْرَةٍ مِنْهُ يَشُدُّ بِهَا صُلْبَهُ وَ ثَوْبٍ يُوَارِي بِهِ عَوْرَتَهُ مِنْ أَغْلَظِ مَا يَجِدُ وَ أَخْشَنِهِ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ فِيمَا لَا بُدَّ لَهُ مِنْهُ ثِقَةٌ وَ لَا رَجَاءٌ فَوَقَعَتْ ثِقَتُهُ وَ رَجَاؤُهُ عَلَى خَالِقِ الْأَشْيَاءِ فَجَدَّ وَ اجْتَهَدَ وَ أَتْعَبَ بَدَنَهُ حَتَّى بَدَتِ الْأَضْلَاعُ وَ غَارَتِ الْعَيْنَانِ فَأَبْدَلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ قُوَّةً فِي بَدَنِهِ وَ شِدَّةً فِي عَقْلِهِ وَ مَا ذُخِرَ لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ أَكْثَرُ فَارْفُضِ الدُّنْيَا فَإِنَّ حُبَّ الدُّنْيَا يُعْمِي وَ يُصِمُّ وَ يُبْكِمُ وَ يُذِلُّ الرِّقَابَ فَتَدَارَكْ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ عُمُرِكَ وَ لَا تَقُلْ غَداً أَوْ بَعْدَ غَدٍ فَإِنَّمَا هَلَكَ مَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكَ بِإِقَامَتِهِمْ عَلَى الْأَمَانِيِّ وَ التَّسْوِيفِ حَتَّى أَتَاهُمْ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ بَغْتَةً وَ هُمْ غَافِلُونَ فَنُقِلُوا عَلَى أَعْوَادِهِمْ إِلَى قُبُورِهِمُ الْمُظْلِمَةِ الضَّيِّقَةِ وَ قَدْ أَسْلَمَهُمُ الْأَوْلَادُ وَ الْأَهْلُونَ فَانْقَطِعْ إِلَى اللَّهِ بِقَلْبٍ مُنِيبٍ مِنْ رَفْضِ الدُّنْيَا وَ عَزْمٍ لَيْسَ فِيهِ انْكِسَارٌ وَ لَا انْخِزَالٌ أَعَانَنَا اللَّهُ وَ إِيَّاكَ عَلَى طَاعَتِهِ وَ وَفَّقَنَا اللَّهُ وَ إِيَّاكَ لِمَرْضَاتِهِ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, and someone else, from Talha Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘An example of the world is like an example of the water of the ocean. Every time it is drunk from, the thirst increases until it kills him (who drinks it)’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha who said, ‘I heard Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Isa<sup>as</sup> Bin Maryam<sup>as</sup> said to the disciples: ‘O Children of Israel! Do not despair upon what is lost by you from the world, just as the people of the world do not despair upon what is lost by them from their Religion as long as they secure their world’.

text: Al HHusayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washha, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Ubeyda, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying: “By My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty, and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Magnificence, and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Exaltedness, and the Loftiness of My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Poisition! No servant would prefer My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Desires over his own desires except that I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Suffice upon his losses, and the skies and the earth would guarantee his sustenance, and I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would be Backing him in business with every businessman’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:62
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ وَ عِزَّتِي وَ جَلَالِي وَ عَظَمَتِي وَ عُلُوِّي وَ ارْتِفَاعِ مَكَانِي لَا يُؤْثِرُ عَبْدٌ هَوَايَ عَلَى هَوَى نَفْسِهِ إِلَّا كَفَفْتُ عَلَيْهِ ضَيْعَتَهُ وَ ضَمَّنْتُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَ الْأَرْضَ رِزْقَهُ وَ كُنْتُ لَهُ مِنْ وَرَاءِ تِجَارَةِ كُلِّ تَاجِرٍ .
citation.translation: Al HHusayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washha, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Ubeyda, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying: “By My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty, and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Magnificence, and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Exaltedness, and the Loftiness of My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Poisition! No servant would prefer My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Desires over his own desires except that I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Suffice upon his losses, and the skies and the earth would guarantee his sustenance, and I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would be Backing him in business with every businessman’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “By My<sup>azwj</sup> Honour, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Majesty, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Magnificence, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Glory, and the Loftiness of My<sup>azwj</sup> Exaltedness! No believing servant would prefer My<sup>azwj</sup> Desires over his own desires with regards to anything from the matters of the world, except that I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Make richness to be in his soul, and Concern him regarding his Hereafter, and the skies and the earth would guarantee his sustenance, and I<sup>azwj</sup> would be for him behind a trade with every trader’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:62

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ammar Bin Marwan, from Zay Bin Al Shahham, from Amro Bin Hilal who said, Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘Beware of aspiring your vision towards the one who is above you, and suffice with what Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said to Hisazwj Prophetsaww [9:55] Let not then their property and their children astound you. And Heazwj Said [20:131] And do not stretch your eyes after that with which We have Provided wedded pairs of them, blossoms of the life of the world. So if anything from that enters into you, then remember the life of Rasool-Allahsaww, So rather, hisasws provision was the barley and the sweetness of the dates, and hissaww fuel was the firewood, when hesaww found it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:63
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) إِيَّاكَ أَنْ تُطْمِحَ بَصَرَكَ إِلَى مَنْ فَوْقَكَ فَكَفَى بِمَا قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لِنَبِيِّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَلا تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَ لا أَوْلادُهُمْ وَ قَالَ وَ لا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلى ما مَتَّعْنا بِهِ أَزْواجاً مِنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا فَإِنْ دَخَلَكَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْ‏ءٌ فَاذْكُرْ عَيْشَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَإِنَّمَا كَانَ قُوتُهُ الشَّعِيرَ وَ حَلْوَاهُ التَّمْرَ وَ وَقُودُهُ السَّعَفَ إِذَا وَجَدَهُ .

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Bin Aamir, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, altogether from Al Washha, from Ahmad Bin Aiz, from Abu Khadeeja Ali Bin Mukram, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who asked us<sup>saww</sup>, we<sup>asws</sup> gave it to him, and the one who managed without (asking), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Enriched him’’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:63
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ سَأَلَنَا أَعْطَيْنَاهُ وَ مَنِ اسْتَغْنَى أَغْنَاهُ اللَّهُ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bi nIsa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al Haysam Bin Waqid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who was satisfied from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with the less from the livelihood, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be Pleased with him from the less, from the deeds’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:63
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ رَضِيَ مِنَ اللَّهِ بِالْيَسِيرِ مِنَ الْمَعَاشِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ بِالْيَسِيرِ مِنَ الْعَمَلِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bi nIsa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al Haysam Bin Waqid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who was satisfied from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with the less from the livelihood, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be Pleased with him from the less, from the deeds’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/323)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is written in the Torah: “O son of Adam<sup>as</sup>! Become howsoever you desire to. Just as you sow, so shall you reap”! The one who was pleased from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with the little from the sustenance, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Accept the less deeds from him. The one who was pleased with the less from the Permissible (means), his expenditure would be light, and his earnings would be pure, and he would be outside from the boundary of the immoralities’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:63
citation.arabic_text: مَكْتُوبٌ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ ابْنَ آدَمَ كُنْ كَيْفَ شِئْتَ كَمَا تَدِينُ تُدَانُ مَنْ رَضِيَ مِنَ اللَّهِ بِالْقَلِيلِ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ قَبِلَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ الْيَسِيرَ مِنَ الْعَمَلِ وَ مَنْ رَضِيَ بِالْيَسِيرِ مِنَ الْحَلَالِ خَفَّتْ مَئُونَتُهُ وَ زَكَتْ مَكْسَبَتُهُ وَ خَرَجَ مِنْ حَدِّ الْفُجُورِ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Arafat, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who is not content from the sustenance except with a lot, would not be sufficed with from the deeds except a lot; and the one who suffices from the little sustenance, so he would be sufficed from the little deeds’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:63
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ لَمْ يُقْنِعْهُ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ إِلَّا الْكَثِيرُ لَمْ يَكْفِهِ مِنَ الْعَمَلِ إِلَّا الْكَثِيرُ وَ مَنْ كَفَاهُ مِنَ الرِّزْقِ الْقَلِيلُ فَإِنَّهُ يَكْفِيهِ مِنَ الْعَمَلِ الْقَلِيلُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Arafat, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who is not content from the sustenance except with a lot, would not be sufficed with from the deeds except a lot; and the one who suffices from the little sustenance, so he would be sufficed from the little deeds’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/324)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘If you want from the world what would suffice you, so the least of what is in it would suffice you, and if you, rather, wanted what would not suffice you, so everything what is in it would not suffice you’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:63
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( صلوات الله عليه ) يَقُولُ ابْنَ آدَمَ إِنْ كُنْتَ تُرِيدُ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا مَا يَكْفِيكَ فَإِنَّ أَيْسَرَ مَا فِيهَا يَكْفِيكَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ إِنَّمَا تُرِيدُ مَا لَا يَكْفِيكَ فَإِنَّ كُلَّ مَا فِيهَا لَا يَكْفِيكَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘If you want from the world what would suffice you, so the least of what is in it would suffice you, and if you, rather, wanted what would not suffice you, so everything what is in it would not suffice you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/325)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Muhammad Al Asady, from Alim Bin Mukram, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The (financial) state of a man from the companions of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> became difficult, so his wife said to him, ‘If only you would go to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and ask him<sup>saww</sup>’. So he came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So when the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> saw him, said: ‘The one who asks us<sup>saww</sup>, we<sup>saww</sup> give to him, but the one who manages without (asking), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Enrich him’. So the man said, ‘He<sup>saww</sup> did not mean anyone apart from me’. So he returned to his wife and let her know. So she said ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> is a ‘Bashr’ (person), so let him<sup>saww</sup> know of it’. So he went over to him<sup>saww</sup>. So when Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> saw him, he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who asks us<sup>saww</sup>, we<sup>saww</sup> give to him, and the one who manages without (asking), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Enrich him’, to the extent that the man did that three times. Then the man went away, and he borrowed a pick-axe, then went to the mountain and ascended it, and cut some firewood. Then he came with it and sold it for half a Mudd (750 gms.) of flour and he returned with it. So he ate it, then went (again) the next day and came with a lot of that, and he sold it. So he did not cease working and gathering (money) until he bought a pick-axe. Then he gathered (money) until he bought two young camels and a slave. Then he was enriched to the extent that he was affluent. So he came over to the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> and let him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> know how he had come to ask him, and how the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> made him hear (the advice). So the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> told you, the one who asks us<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, we give it to him, but the one who manages (without asking), Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Enrich him’’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:63
citation.arabic_text: اشْتَدَّتْ حَالُ رَجُلٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقَالَتْ لَهُ امْرَأَتُهُ لَوْ أَتَيْتَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَسَأَلْتَهُ فَجَاءَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَلَمَّا رَآهُ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَالَ مَنْ سَأَلَنَا أَعْطَيْنَاهُ وَ مَنِ اسْتَغْنَى أَغْنَاهُ اللَّهُ فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ مَا يَعْنِي غَيْرِي فَرَجَعَ إِلَى امْرَأَتِهِ فَأَعْلَمَهَا فَقَالَتْ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بَشَرٌ فَأَعْلِمْهُ فَأَتَاهُ فَلَمَّا رَآهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَالَ مَنْ سَأَلَنَا أَعْطَيْنَاهُ وَ مَنِ اسْتَغْنَى أَغْنَاهُ اللَّهُ حَتَّى فَعَلَ الرَّجُلُ ذَلِكَ ثَلَاثاً ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ الرَّجُلُ فَاسْتَعَارَ مِعْوَلًا ثُمَّ أَتَى الْجَبَلَ فَصَعِدَهُ فَقَطَعَ حَطَباً ثُمَّ جَاءَ بِهِ فَبَاعَهُ بِنِصْفِ مُدٍّ مِنْ دَقِيقٍ فَرَجَعَ بِهِ فَأَكَلَهُ ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ مِنَ الْغَدِ فَجَاءَ بِأَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَبَاعَهُ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَعْمَلُ وَ يَجْمَعُ حَتَّى اشْتَرَى مِعْوَلًا ثُمَّ جَمَعَ حَتَّى اشْتَرَى بَكْرَيْنِ وَ غُلَاماً ثُمَّ أَثْرَى حَتَّى أَيْسَرَ فَجَاءَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَأَعْلَمَهُ كَيْفَ جَاءَ يَسْأَلُهُ وَ كَيْفَ سَمِعَ النَّبِيَّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قُلْتُ لَكَ مَنْ سَأَلَنَا أَعْطَيْنَاهُ وَ مَنِ اسْتَغْنَى أَغْنَاهُ اللَّهُ .

So he came over to the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> and let him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> know how he had come to ask him, and how the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> made him hear (the advice). So the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> told you, the one who asks us<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, we give it to him, but the one who manages (without asking), Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Enrich him’’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/325)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Al Hakam Bin Al Husayn Bin Al Furat, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who wants to be needless of the people, so let him rely upon what is in the Hands of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> rather than what is in the hands of the people’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَكُونَ أَغْنَى النَّاسِ فَلْيَكُنْ بِمَا فِي يَدِ اللَّهِ أَوْثَقَ مِنْهُ بِمَا فِي يَدِ غَيْرِهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Al Hakam Bin Al Husayn Bin Al Furat, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who wants to be needless of the people, so let him rely upon what is in the Hands of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> rather than what is in the hands of the people’.

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, or Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who is content with what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Graced him, so he is from the richest of the people’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ قَنِعَ بِمَا رَزَقَهُ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ مِنْ أَغْنَى النَّاسِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, or Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who is content with what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Graced him, so he is from the richest of the people’.

text: From, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bakeyr, from Hamza Bin Humran who said, ‘A man complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that he seeks, so he attains but is not content and his heart contends with him to what is more than it, and he said, ‘Teach me something I can be content with it’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was what suffices you, it would enrich you what is the least of what is in it, and if it was what does not suffice you, it would not enrich you, so (even) whatever is in it (the world) would not suffice you’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:63
citation.arabic_text: شَكَا رَجُلٌ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَنَّهُ يَطْلُبُ فَيُصِيبُ وَ لَا يَقْنَعُ وَ تُنَازِعُهُ نَفْسُهُ إِلَى مَا هُوَ أَكْثَرُ مِنْهُ وَ قَالَ عَلِّمْنِي شَيْئاً أَنْتَفِعْ بِهِ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنْ كَانَ مَا يَكْفِيكَ يُغْنِيكَ فَأَدْنَى مَا فِيهَا يُغْنِيكَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ مَا يَكْفِيكَ لَا يُغْنِيكَ فَكُلُّ مَا فِيهَا لَا يُغْنِيكَ .

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:63
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) مَنْ رَضِيَ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا بِمَا يُجْزِيهِ كَانَ أَيْسَرُ مَا فِيهَا يَكْفِيهِ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَرْضَ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا بِمَا يُجْزِيهِ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهَا شَيْ‏ءٌ يَكْفِيهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from a number of our companions, from Hanan Bin Sadeyr, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who is pleased from the world with whatever his apportionment is, the least of what is in it would suffice him; and the one who is not pleased from the world with what his apportionment is, there is nothing in it which would suffice him’.

So he is patient upon it, his death being hastened, and few are his inheritors and few are his mourners’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) اللَّهُمَّ ارْزُقْ مُحَمَّداً وَ آلَ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ مَنْ أَحَبَّ مُحَمَّداً وَ آلَ مُحَمَّدٍ الْعَفَافَ وَ الْكَفَافَ وَ ارْزُقْ مَنْ أَبْغَضَ مُحَمَّداً وَ آلَ مُحَمَّدٍ الْمَالَ وَ الْوَلَدَ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Nowfaly, (It has been narrated) raising it to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasoool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> passed by a camel shepherd, so he<sup>saww</sup> sent to him to quench him<sup>saww</sup>, but he said, ‘As for what is in their udders, so it is for their morning, and as for what is in our containers, so it is for their evening’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Increase his wealth and his children’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> passed by a sheep shepherd. So he<sup>saww</sup> sent for him to quench him<sup>saww</sup>. So he milked for him<sup>saww</sup> whatever was in its udders, and added to whatever was in his container into the container of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and sent a sheep over to him<sup>saww</sup> and said: ‘This is what is with us, and if you<sup>saww</sup> so love it that we increase it for you<sup>saww</sup>, we shall increase it for you<sup>saww</sup>’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Grace him at the subsistence level’. So one of his<sup>saww</sup> companions said to him<sup>saww</sup>, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! You<sup>saww</sup> supplicated for the one who repulsed you<sup>saww</sup> with a supplication which the generality of us would love, and you<sup>saww</sup> supplicated to the one who relieved you<sup>saww</sup> of your<sup>saww</sup> need with a supplication which we all would dislike’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What is little and just enough is better than what is more and diverting. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Grace Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, the subsistence’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:64
citation.arabic_text: مَرَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بِرَاعِي إِبِلٍ فَبَعَثَ يَسْتَسْقِيهِ فَقَالَ أَمَّا مَا فِي ضُرُوعِهَا فَصَبُوحُ الْحَيِّ وَ أَمَّا مَا فِي آنِيَتِنَا فَغَبُوقُهُمْ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) اللَّهُمَّ أَكْثِرْ مَالَهُ وَ وُلْدَهُ ثُمَّ مَرَّ بِرَاعِي غَنَمٍ فَبَعَثَ إِلَيْهِ يَسْتَسْقِيهِ فَحَلَبَ لَهُ مَا فِي ضُرُوعِهَا وَ أَكْفَأَ مَا فِي إِنَائِهِ فِي إِنَاءِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ بَعَثَ إِلَيْهِ بِشَاةٍ وَ قَالَ هَذَا مَا عِنْدَنَا وَ إِنْ أَحْبَبْتَ أَنْ نَزِيدَكَ زِدْنَاكَ قَالَ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) اللَّهُمَّ ارْزُقْهُ الْكَفَافَ فَقَالَ لَهُ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِهِ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ دَعَوْتَ لِلَّذِي رَدَّكَ بِدُعَاءٍ عَامَّتُنَا نُحِبُّهُ وَ دَعَوْتَ لِلَّذِي أَسْعَفَكَ بِحَاجَتِكَ بِدُعَاءٍ كُلُّنَا نَكْرَهُهُ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِنَّ مَا قَلَّ وَ كَفَى خَيْرٌ مِمَّا كَثُرَ وَ أَلْهَى اللَّهُمَّ ارْزُقْ مُحَمَّداً وَ آلَ مُحَمَّدٍ الْكَفَافَ .

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Bakr Bin Muhammad Al Azdy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “The most blissful of My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> friends in My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Presence is a believing servant with a share from righteousness, good worship of his Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and he worships Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> in the secrecy, and he was hidden among the people, so he was not pointed at by the fingers, and his sustenance was at subsistence level. citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:64
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِنَّ مِنْ أَغْبَطِ أَوْلِيَائِي عِنْدِي عَبْداً مُؤْمِناً ذَا حَظٍّ مِنْ صَلَاحٍ أَحْسَنَ عِبَادَةَ رَبِّهِ وَ عَبَدَ اللَّهَ فِي السَّرِيرَةِ وَ كَانَ غَامِضاً فِي النَّاسِ فَلَمْ يُشَرْ إِلَيْهِ بِالْأَصَابِعِ وَ كَانَ رِزْقُهُ كَفَافاً فَصَبَرَ عَلَيْهِ فَعَجَّلَتْ بِهِ الْمَنِيَّةُ فَقَلَّ تُرَاثُهُ وَ قَلَّتْ بَوَاكِيهِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Bakr Bin Muhammad Al Azdy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “The most blissful of My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> friends in My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Presence is a believing servant with a share from righteousness, good worship of his Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and he worships Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> in the secrecy, and he was hidden among the people, so he was not pointed at by the fingers, and his sustenance was at subsistence level. So he was patient upon it, and the death hastened to him, and few were his inheritors, and few were his mourners’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (332/ 8)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Numan who said, ‘Hamza Bin Humran narrated to me saying, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Whenever one of you intends the goodness, so he should not delay it, for the servant sometimes prays the Salāt or Fasts for the day, and it is said to him: ‘Do whatever you so desire to after it, for Allahazwj has Forgiven (your sins) for you’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:65
citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي حَمْزَةُ بْنُ حُمْرَانَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِذَا هَمَّ أَحَدُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ فَلَا يُؤَخِّرْهُ فَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ رُبَّمَا صَلَّى الصَّلَاةَ أَوْ صَامَ الْيَوْمَ فَيُقَالُ لَهُ اعْمَلْ مَا شِئْتَ بَعْدَهَا فَقَدْ غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَكَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Numan who said, ‘Hamza Bin Humran narrated to me saying, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Whenever one of you intends the goodness, so he should not delay it, for the servant sometimes prays the Salāt or Fasts for the day, and it is said to him: ‘Do whatever you so desire to after it, for Allahazwj has Forgiven (your sins) for you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/333)

text: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Jameela who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Begin your days with goodness, and dictate upon your preservers (Two recording Angels), goodness at the beginning of the day, and goodness at the end of it, He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Forgive (your sins) for you in what is between that, Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Willing’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:65
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) افْتَتِحُوا نَهَارَكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ وَ أَمْلُوا عَلَى حَفَظَتِكُمْ فِي أَوَّلِهِ خَيْراً وَ فِي آخِرِهِ خَيْراً يُغْفَرْ لَكُمْ مَا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Jameela who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Begin your days with goodness, and dictate upon your preservers (Two recording Angels), goodness at the beginning of the day, and goodness at the end of it, He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Forgive (your sins) for you in what is between that, Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Willing’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (334/ 8)

text: From him, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Murazim Bin Hakeym, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Whenever you are intending with a goodness, so hasten, for you do not know what might occur’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:65
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَبِي يَقُولُ إِذَا هَمَمْتَ بِخَيْرٍ فَبَادِرْ فَإِنَّكَ لَا تَدْرِي مَا يَحْدُثُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Murazim Bin Hakeym, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Whenever you are intending with a goodness, so hasten, for you do not know what might occur’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/334)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Loves from the goodness what is hastened (with)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:65
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ مَا يُعَجَّلُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Loves from the goodness what is hastened (with)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/335)

text: A number of companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Bashir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever you intend something from the goodness, so do not delay it, for the servant would Fast on the hot day intending what is in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Free him from the Fire due to it, and you should not belittle what you could get closer with to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and even though it may be part of a date’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:65
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا أَرَدْتَ شَيْئاً مِنَ الْخَيْرِ فَلَا تُؤَخِّرْهُ فَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ يَصُومُ الْيَوْمَ الْحَارَّ يُرِيدُ مَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ فَيُعْتِقُهُ اللَّهُ بِهِ مِنَ النَّارِ وَ لَا تَسْتَقِلَّ مَا يُتَقَرَّبُ بِهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ لَوْ شِقَّ تَمْرَةٍ .
citation.translation: A number of companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Bashir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever you intend something from the goodness, so do not delay it, for the servant would Fast on the hot day intending what is in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Free him from the Fire due to it, and you should not belittle what you could get closer with to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and even though it may be part of a date’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/335)

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who intends a goodness, so let him hasten it and not delay it, for sometimes the servant performs the deed, so Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blessed and High is Saying: “I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> have Forgiven (your sins) for you and will not Write anything against you, ever!”; and the one who intends an evil, so he should not hasten it, for sometimes the servant would perform the evil, so Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, Glorious is He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, Sees him, and He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Saying: “No, by My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty, I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> will not Forgive (your sins) for you after it, ever!”’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:65
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ هَمَّ بِخَيْرٍ فَلْيُعَجِّلْهُ وَ لَا يُؤَخِّرْهُ فَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ رُبَّمَا عَمِلَ الْعَمَلَ فَيَقُولُ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى قَدْ غَفَرْتُ لَكَ وَ لَا أَكْتُبُ عَلَيْكَ شَيْئاً أَبَداً وَ مَنْ هَمَّ بِسَيِّئَةٍ فَلَا يَعْمَلْهَا فَإِنَّهُ رُبَّمَا عَمِلَ الْعَبْدُ السَّيِّئَةَ فَيَرَاهُ اللَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ فَيَقُولُ لَا وَ عِزَّتِي وَ جَلَالِي لَا أَغْفِرُ لَكَ بَعْدَهَا أَبَداً .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who intends a goodness, so let him hasten it and not delay it, for sometimes the servant performs the deed, so Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blessed and High is Saying: “I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> have Forgiven (your sins) for you and will not Write anything against you, ever!”; and the one who intends an evil, so he should not hasten it, for sometimes the servant would perform the evil, so Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, Glorious is He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, Sees him, and He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Saying: “No, by My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty, I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> will not Forgive (your sins) for you after it, ever!”’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/335)

text: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever you intend for anything from the goodness, so do not delay it, for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Notify upon the servant while he is upon something from the obedience, so He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Saying: ‘By My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty! I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> will not Punish you after it, ever!” And when he intends for an evil, but he does not do it, so sometimes Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Notify upon the servant while he is upon something from the disobedience, so He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Saying: “By My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My <sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty! I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> will not Forgive (your sins) for you after it, ever!”’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:65
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا هَمَمْتَ بِشَيْ‏ءٍ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ فَلَا تُؤَخِّرْهُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ رُبَّمَا اطَّلَعَ عَلَى الْعَبْدِ وَ هُوَ عَلَى شَيْ‏ءٍ مِنَ الطَّاعَةِ فَيَقُولُ وَ عِزَّتِي وَ جَلَالِي لَا أُعَذِّبُكَ بَعْدَهَا أَبَداً وَ إِذَا هَمَمْتَ بِسَيِّئَةٍ فَلَا تَعْمَلْهَا فَإِنَّهُ رُبَّمَا اطَّلَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْعَبْدِ وَ هُوَ عَلَى شَيْ‏ءٍ مِنَ الْمَعْصِيَةِ فَيَقُولُ وَ عِزَّتِي وَ جَلَالِي لَا أَغْفِرُ لَكَ بَعْدَهَا أَبَداً .
citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever you intend for anything from the goodness, so do not delay it, for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Notify upon the servant while he is upon something from the obedience, so He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Saying: ‘By My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty! I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> will not Punish you after it, ever!” And when he intends for an evil, but he does not do it, so sometimes Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Notify upon the servant while he is upon something from the disobedience, so He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Saying: “By My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My <sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty! I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> will not Forgive (your sins) for you after it, ever!”’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (336/ 8)

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad Bin Humran, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you intends a goodness, or a maintenance of relationship, so upon his right and upon his left would be Satans<sup>la</sup>, therefore, let him hasten and not refrain from that’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:65
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا هَمَّ أَحَدُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ أَوْ صِلَةٍ فَإِنَّ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ شِمَالِهِ شَيْطَانَيْنِ فَلْيُبَادِرْ لَا يَكُفَّاهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad Bin Humran, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you intends a goodness, or a maintenance of relationship, so upon his right and upon his left would be Satans<sup>la</sup>, therefore, let him hasten and not refrain from that’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (336/ 8)

text: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who intends for formatting from the goodness, so let him hasten it, for in everything where is a delay, so for the Satans<sup>la</sup> therein is a respite’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:65
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَنْ هَمَّ بِشَيْ‏ءٍ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ فَلْيُعَجِّلْهُ فَإِنَّ كُلَّ شَيْ‏ءٍ فِيهِ تَأْخِيرٌ فَإِنَّ لِلشَّيْطَانِ فِيهِ نَظْرَةً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who intends for formatting from the goodness, so let him hasten it, for in everything where is a delay, so for the Satans<sup>la</sup> therein is a respite’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (337/ 8)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Weighs down the goodness upon the people of the world like its weighing down would be in their Scales on the Day of Judgement; and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Lightens the evil upon the people of the world like its lightness would be in their Scales on the Day of Judgement’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:65
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ ثَقَّلَ الْخَيْرَ عَلَى أَهْلِ الدُّنْيَا كَثِقْلِهِ فِي مَوَازِينِهِمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ خَفَّفَ الشَّرَّ عَلَى أَهْلِ الدُّنْيَا كَخِفَّتِهِ فِي مَوَازِينِهِمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Weighs down the goodness upon the people of the world like its weighing down would be in their Scales on the Day of Judgement; and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Lightens the evil upon the people of the world like its lightness would be in their Scales on the Day of Judgement’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (339/ 8)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Hassan Bin Hamza, from his grandfather, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said at the end of his<sup>saww</sup> sermon: ‘Toba’ (a Blessed tree in Paradise) is for the one who makes good his manners, and cleans up his temper, and corrects his secretive deeds, and improves his unconcealed deeds, and spends the excess from his wealth, and withholds the excess from his words, and is fair with the people from himself’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَقُولُ فِي آخِرِ خُطْبَتِهِ طُوبَى لِمَنْ طَابَ خُلُقُهُ وَ طَهُرَتْ سَجِيَّتُهُ وَ صَلَحَتْ سَرِيرَتُهُ وَ حَسُنَتْ عَلَانِيَتُهُ وَ أَنْفَقَ الْفَضْلَ مِنْ مَالِهِ وَ أَمْسَكَ الْفَضْلَ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ وَ أَنْصَفَ النَّاسَ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Hassan Bin Hamza, from his grandfather, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said at the end of his<sup>saww</sup> sermon: ‘Toba’ (a Blessed tree in Paradise) is for the one who makes good his manners, and cleans up his temper, and corrects his secretive deeds, and improves his unconcealed deeds, and spends the excess from his wealth, and withholds the excess from his words, and is fair with the people from himself’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (340/ 8)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who guarantees four (matters) to me<sup>asws</sup>, (I<sup>asws</sup> will guarantee) four houses (for him) in the Paradise – Spends (in charity) and does not fear the poverty, and discloses the greetings in the world, and leaves the disputing even if he was right, and be fair with the people from himself’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ يَضْمَنُ لِي أَرْبَعَةً بِأَرْبَعَةِ أَبْيَاتٍ فِي الْجَنَّةِ أَنْفِقْ وَ لَا تَخَفْ فَقْراً وَ أَفْشِ السَّلَامَ فِي الْعَالَمِ وَ اتْرُكِ الْمِرَاءَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ مُحِقّاً وَ أَنْصِفِ النَّاسَ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who guarantees four (matters) to me<sup>asws</sup>, (I<sup>asws</sup> will guarantee) four houses (for him) in the Paradise – Spends (in charity) and does not fear the poverty, and discloses the greetings in the world, and leaves the disputing even if he was right, and be fair with the people from himself’.

text: From him, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Jaroud Abu Al Munzir who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The chief of the deeds are three – Fairness with the people from yourself until you are not pleased with something except you are pleased for with the like of it; and your equalising with the brother in the wealth; and remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon every state. (This is) not (saying), ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest’, only, but, when something comes up to you which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Commanded with, you take to it, or when something comes upon you which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Forbidden from, you leave it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ سَيِّدُ الْأَعْمَالِ ثَلَاثَةٌ إِنْصَافُ النَّاسِ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ حَتَّى لَا تَرْضَى بِشَيْ‏ءٍ إِلَّا رَضِيتَ لَهُمْ مِثْلَهُ وَ مُوَاسَاتُكَ الْأَخَ فِي الْمَالِ وَ ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ لَيْسَ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ فَقَطْ وَ لَكِنْ إِذَا وَرَدَ عَلَيْكَ شَيْ‏ءٌ أَمَرَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ بِهِ أَخَذْتَ بِهِ أَوْ إِذَا وَرَدَ عَلَيْكَ شَيْ‏ءٌ نَهَى اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَنْهُ تَرَكْتَهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Jaroud Abu Al Munzir who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The chief of the deeds are three – Fairness with the people from yourself until you are not pleased with something except you are pleased for with the like of it; and your equalising with the brother in the wealth; and remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon every state. (This is) not (saying), ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest’, only, but, when something comes up to you which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Commanded with, you take to it, or when something comes upon you which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Forbidden from, you leave it’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Saqafy, from Ali Bin Al Moalla, from Yahya Bin Ahmad, from Abu Muhammad Al Maysami, from Rowmiyyi Bin Zurara, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said in a speech of his<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Indeed! The one is fair with the people from himself, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would not Increase him in anything except for honour’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فِي كَلَامٍ لَهُ أَلَا إِنَّهُ مَنْ يُنْصِفِ النَّاسَ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ لَمْ يَزِدْهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا عِزّاً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Saqafy, from Ali Bin Al Moalla, from Yahya Bin Ahmad, from Abu Muhammad Al Maysami, from Rowmiyyi Bin Zurara, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said in a speech of his<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Indeed! The one is fair with the people from himself, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would not Increase him in anything except for honour’.

text: Rom him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (types), they would be the closest of the people to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic on the Day of Judgement until He<sup>azwj</sup> is Free from the Reckoning – a man whose power does not invite him, during the state of his anger, to wrong the one who in under his hand; and a man who walks (mediates) between two, but he does not incline with one of them against the other with (even) a barley seed; and a man who speaks with the truth in what is for him, and (what is) against him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: ثَلَاثَةٌ هُمْ أَقْرَبُ الْخَلْقِ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ مِنَ الْحِسَابِ رَجُلٌ لَمْ تَدْعُهُ قُدْرَةٌ فِي حَالِ غَضَبِهِ إِلَى أَنْ يَحِيفَ عَلَى مَنْ تَحْتَ يَدِهِ وَ رَجُلٌ مَشَى بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ فَلَمْ يَمِلْ مَعَ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَى الْآخَرِ بِشَعِيرَةٍ وَ رَجُلٌ قَالَ بِالْحَقِّ فِيمَا لَهُ وَ عَلَيْهِ .
citation.translation: Rom him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (types), they would be the closest of the people to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic on the Day of Judgement until He<sup>azwj</sup> is Free from the Reckoning – a man whose power does not invite him, during the state of his anger, to wrong the one who in under his hand; and a man who walks (mediates) between two, but he does not incline with one of them against the other with (even) a barley seed; and a man who speaks with the truth in what is for him, and (what is) against him’.

text: From him, from his father, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Zurara, from Al Hassan Al Bazzaz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> in a Hadeeth of his<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> inform you with the most difficult of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Imposed upon His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures?’, and he<sup>asws</sup> mentioned three things, the first of these being: ‘Fairness with the people from yourself’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: فِي حَدِيثٍ لَهُ أَ لَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِأَشَدِّ مَا فَرَضَ اللَّهُ عَلَى خَلْقِهِ فَذَكَرَ ثَلَاثَةَ أَشْيَاءَ أَوَّلُهَا إِنْصَافُ النَّاسِ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Zurara, from Al Hassan Al Bazzaz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> in a Hadeeth of his<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> inform you with the most difficult of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Imposed upon His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures?’, and he<sup>asws</sup> mentioned three things, the first of these being: ‘Fairness with the people from yourself’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The chief of the deeds is fairness with the people from yourself, and equalising with the brother for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and mentioning Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic upon every state’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) سَيِّدُ الْأَعْمَالِ إِنْصَافُ النَّاسِ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ وَ مُوَاسَاةُ الْأَخِ فِي اللَّهِ وَ ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The chief of the deeds is fairness with the people from yourself, and equalising with the brother for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and mentioning Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic upon every state’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/345)

text: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Zurara, from Al Hassan Al Bazzaz who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> inform you with the most difficult of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Imposed upon His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Fairness with the people from yourself, and your equalizing your brother, and mentioning Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in every place. But, I<sup>asws</sup> am not saying, (that you should be saying), ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest’, and even though this is from that, but remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Majestic and Mighty in every place, when you are confronted upon obedience of upon disobedience’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَ لَا أُخْبِرُكَ بِأَشَدِّ مَا فَرَضَ اللَّهُ عَلَى خَلْقِهِ ثَلَاثٌ قُلْتُ بَلَى قَالَ إِنْصَافُ النَّاسِ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ وَ مُوَاسَاتُكَ أَخَاكَ وَ ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ فِي كُلِّ مَوْطِنٍ أَمَا إِنِّي لَا أَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ هَذَا مِنْ ذَاكَ وَ لَكِنْ ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ جَلَّ وَ عَزَّ فِي كُلِّ مَوْطِنٍ إِذَا هَجَمْتَ عَلَى طَاعَةٍ أَوْ عَلَى مَعْصِيَةٍ .

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Asama who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Believer is not Tested with anything more difficult upon him than three characteristics depriving him’. It was said, ‘And what are these?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The equalisation regarding what is in his hands, and the fairness from himself, and remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> a lot. But, I<sup>asws</sup> am not saying (that one should be saying), ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Praise for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, but remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during what is Permissible for him, and remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during what is Prohibited upon him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا ابْتُلِيَ الْمُؤْمِنُ بِشَيْ‏ءٍ أَشَدَّ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ خِصَالٍ ثَلَاثٍ يُحْرَمُهَا قِيلَ وَ مَا هُنَّ قَالَ الْمُوَاسَاةُ فِي ذَاتِ يَدِهِ وَ الْإِنْصَافُ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ وَ ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ كَثِيراً أَمَا إِنِّي لَا أَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَ لَكِنْ ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ عِنْدَ مَا أَحَلَّ لَهُ وَ ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ عِنْدَ مَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْهِ .
citation.translation: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Asama who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Believer is not Tested with anything more difficult upon him than three characteristics depriving him’. It was said, ‘And what are these?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The equalisation regarding what is in his hands, and the fairness from himself, and remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> a lot. But, I<sup>asws</sup> am not saying (that one should be saying), ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Praise for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, but remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during what is Permissible for him, and remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during what is Prohibited upon him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (8/346)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad bin Abu Abdullah, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from his father, from his grandfather Abu Al Balaad, raising it, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A Bedouin came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he<sup>saww</sup> wanted (to go on to) one of his<sup>saww</sup> military expeditions. So he grabbed one of the reins of his<sup>saww</sup> riding animal, and he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Teach me a deed by which I can enter the Paradise’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whatever you love the people to come to you with, so go to them with it, and whatever you dislike the people coming to you with, so do not go to them with it’. He freed the way of the riding animal’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: جَاءَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ هُوَ يُرِيدُ بَعْضَ غَزَوَاتِهِ فَأَخَذَ بِغَرْزِ رَاحِلَتِهِ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عَلِّمْنِي عَمَلًا أَدْخُلُ بِهِ الْجَنَّةَ فَقَالَ مَا أَحْبَبْتَ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُ النَّاسُ إِلَيْكَ فَأْتِهِ إِلَيْهِمْ وَ مَا كَرِهْتَ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُ النَّاسُ إِلَيْكَ فَلَا تَأْتِهِ إِلَيْهِمْ خَلِّ سَبِيلَ الرَّاحِلَةِ .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, from Abdul Kareem, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The justice is sweeter than the water poured upon the thirsty one. How extensive is the justice when there is justice in it (in a matter), and even if it is little’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: الْعَدْلُ أَحْلَى مِنَ الْمَاءِ يُصِيبُهُ الظَّمْآنُ مَا أَوْسَعَ الْعَدْلَ إِذَا عُدِلَ فِيهِ وَ إِنْ قَلَّ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, from Abdul Kareem, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The justice is sweeter than the water poured upon the thirsty one. How extensive is the justice when there is justice in it (in a matter), and even if it is little’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (347/ 8)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who is fair with the people from himself, would be pleased with judging for others’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَنْصَفَ النَّاسَ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ رُضِيَ بِهِ حَكَماً لِغَيْرِهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who is fair with the people from himself, would be pleased with judging for others’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (348/ 8)

text: Muhammad in Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Yunus Bin Imran Bin Maysam, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto Adam<sup>as</sup>: “I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Gather the Speech for you in four Sentences”. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! And what are these?’ He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “One for Me<sup>azwj</sup>, and one for You<sup>as</sup>, and one regarding what is between Me<sup>azwj</sup> and you<sup>as</sup>, and one regarding what is between you<sup>as</sup> and the people”. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! Explain these to me<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> until I<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> know these’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Said: “As for that which is for Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, so worship Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, nor associating anything with Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>; and as for that which is for you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, so I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> shall Recompense you for your<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> deeds with what would you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> would happen to be the most needy to; and as for that which is between Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> and you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, so upon you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> is the supplication and upon Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is the Answering; and as for that which is between you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> and the people, so you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> should be pleased with the people what you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> would be pleased with yourself<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, and dislike for them what you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> would dislike for yourself<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF BELIEF (Emān) AND DISBELIEF (KUFR) (al-Kafi, vol 2), 1:66
