text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘(Initiating) the greeting (السَّلَامُ) is voluntary, and the responding is an Obligation’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) السَّلَامُ تَطَوُّعٌ وَ الرَّدُّ فَرِيضَةٌ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘(Initiating) the greeting (السَّلَامُ) is voluntary, and the responding is an Obligation’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/539)

text: And by this chain, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who begins the speech before the greeting (السَّلَامُ), so do not answer him’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Initiate with the greeting (السَّلَامُ) before the speech. So the one who begins with the speech before the greeting (السَّلَامُ), so do not answer him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ مَنْ بَدَأَ بِالْكَلَامِ قَبْلَ السَّلَامِ فَلَا تُجِيبُوهُ وَ قَالَ ابْدَءُوا بِالسَّلَامِ قَبْلَ الْكَلَامِ فَمَنْ بَدَأَ بِالْكَلَامِ قَبْلَ السَّلَامِ فَلَا تُجِيبُوهُ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who begins the speech before the greeting (السَّلَامُ), so do not answer him’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Initiate with the greeting (السَّلَامُ) before the speech. So the one who begins with the speech before the greeting (السَّلَامُ), so do not answer him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/539)

text: And by this chain, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The closest of the people with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and with His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> is the one who initiates the greeting (السَّلَامُ)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِاللَّهِ وَ بِرَسُولِهِ مَنْ بَدَأَ بِالسَّلَامِ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The closest of the people with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and with His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> is the one who initiates the greeting (السَّلَامُ)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/539)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Abdul Rahman Bin abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It was so that Salman<sup>as</sup> was saying: ‘Offer the Greeting (السَّلَامُ) of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> openly, as for the Greeting (السَّلَامُ) of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> cannot be attained by the unjust’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ سَلْمَانُ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ يَقُولُ أَفْشُوا سَلَامَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ سَلَامَ اللَّهِ لَا يَنَالُ الظَّالِمِينَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Abdul Rahman Bin abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It was so that Salman<sup>as</sup> was saying: ‘Offer the Greeting (السَّلَامُ) of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> openly, as for the Greeting (السَّلَامُ) of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> cannot be attained by the unjust’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/540)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Loves the greeting (السَّلَامُ)’ offered openly (loudly).

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يُحِبُّ إِفْشَاءَ السَّلَامِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Loves the greeting (السَّلَامُ)’ offered openly (loudly).
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/540)

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “The stingy one, is the one who is stingy with the greeting (السَّلَامُ)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ قَالَ إِنَّ الْبَخِيلَ مَنْ يَبْخَلُ بِالسَّلَامِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “The stingy one, is the one who is stingy with the greeting (السَّلَامُ)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/540)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whenever one of you greets (السَّلَامُ), so let him be loud with his greeting. He should not be saying, ‘I greeted but he did not respond to me’, and perhaps he may have greeted and he did not hear it. So whenever one of you responds, so let him be loud with his response, and the one greeting one should not be saying, ‘I greeted, but he did not respond to me’. Then heasws said: ‘It was so that Aliasws was saying: ‘Neither get angry nor anger (others). Openly offer the greetings (loudly) and be nice with your speech, and pray Salāt at nights while the people are sleeping, you would be entering the Paradise in safety’. Then heasws recited the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [59:23] the Giver of peace, the Granter of security, Guardian over all’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا سَلَّمَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَجْهَرْ بِسَلَامِهِ لَا يَقُولُ سَلَّمْتُ فَلَمْ يَرُدُّوا عَلَيَّ وَ لَعَلَّهُ يَكُونُ قَدْ سَلَّمَ وَ لَمْ يُسْمِعْهُمْ فَإِذَا رَدَّ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَجْهَرْ بِرَدِّهِ وَ لَا يَقُولُ الْمُسَلِّمُ سَلَّمْتُ فَلَمْ يَرُدُّوا عَلَيَّ ثُمَّ قَالَ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ لَا تَغْضَبُوا وَ لَا تُغْضِبُوا أَفْشُوا السَّلَامَ وَ أَطِيبُوا الْكَلَامَ وَ صَلُّوا بِاللَّيْلِ وَ النَّاسُ نِيَامٌ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِسَلَامٍ ثُمَّ تَلَا ( عليه السلام ) عَلَيْهِمْ قَوْلَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ السَّلامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whenever one of you greets (السَّلَامُ), so let him be loud with his greeting. He should not be saying, ‘I greeted but he did not respond to me’, and perhaps he may have greeted and he did not hear it. Then heasws recited the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [59:23] the Giver of peace, the Granter of security, Guardian over all’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The initiator with the greeting (السَّلَامُ) is the closest of the people with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: الْبَادِي بِالسَّلَامِ أَوْلَى بِاللَّهِ وَ بِرَسُولِهِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Al hassan Bin Al Munzir who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who says ‘The greetings be upon you’ (السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ), so it would be ten good deeds, and the one who says, ‘The greetings be upon you and the Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’ (السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ), so it is twenty good deeds, and the one who says, ‘The greetings be upon you, and the Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Blessings’ (السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ), so it is thirty good deeds’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ مَنْ قَالَ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ فَهِيَ عَشْرُ حَسَنَاتٍ وَ مَنْ قَالَ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ فَهِيَ عِشْرُونَ حَسَنَةً وَ مَنْ قَالَ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ فَهِيَ ثَلَاثُونَ حَسَنَةً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Al hassan Bin Al Munzir who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who says ‘The greetings be upon you’ (السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ), so it would be ten good deeds, and the one who says, ‘The greetings be upon you and the Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’ (السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ), so it is twenty good deeds, and the one who says, ‘The greetings be upon you, and the Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Blessings’ (السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ), so it is thirty good deeds’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Mansour Bin Hazim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three would be responded upon by the plural response, and even though it may be one (person only) – during the sneeze it is said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you all’, and even if there does not happen to be someone else with him; and the man greets upon the man, so he is saying, ‘The greetings be upon you all’, and the man supplicating for the man, so he is saying, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Grant good health to you all’, and even if he is alone; for there are others (Angels) with him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: ثَلَاثَةٌ تُرَدُّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَدَّ الْجَمَاعَةِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ وَاحِداً عِنْدَ الْعُطَاسِ يُقَالُ يَرْحَمُكُمُ اللَّهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ مَعَهُ غَيْرُهُ وَ الرَّجُلُ يُسَلِّمُ عَلَى الرَّجُلِ فَيَقُولُ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ الرَّجُلُ يَدْعُو لِلرَّجُلِ فَيَقُولُ عَافَاكُمُ اللَّهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ وَاحِداً فَإِنَّ مَعَهُ غَيْرَهُ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/541)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, raising it, said, ‘It was so that Abu Abdullahasws was saying: ‘Three (persons) would not be greeting (السَّلَامُ) – the walker along with the funeral, and the walker to the Friday Salāt, and in the bath house’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ ثَلَاثَةٌ لَا يُسَلَّمُونَ الْمَاشِي مَعَ الْجَنَازَةِ وَ الْمَاشِي إِلَى الْجُمُعَةِ وَ فِي بَيْتِ الْحَمَّامِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, raising it, said, ‘It was so that Abu Abdullahasws was saying: ‘Three (persons) would not be greeting (السَّلَامُ) – the walker along with the funeral, and the walker to the Friday Salāt, and in the bath house’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/541)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Haroun Bin Kharija, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘(It is) from the reverence that you greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the one you meet’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: مِنَ التَّوَاضُعِ أَنْ تُسَلِّمَ عَلَى مَنْ لَقِيتَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Haroun Bin Kharija, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘(It is) from the reverence that you greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the one you meet’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/542)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen Ali<sup>asws</sup> passed by a group of people, so he<sup>asws</sup> greeted (السَّلَامُ) upon them. So they said, ‘Upon you<sup>asws</sup> be the greetings, and Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Blessings, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure’. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said to them: ‘Do not say to us<sup>asws</sup> more than what the Angels said to our<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>as</sup> Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>. But rather, they said, ‘Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Blessings be upon you<sup>as</sup>, the People of the Household’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: مَرَّ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) بِقَوْمٍ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالُوا عَلَيْكَ السَّلَامُ وَ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ وَ مَغْفِرَتُهُ وَ رِضْوَانُهُ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تُجَاوِزُوا بِنَا مِثْلَ مَا قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ لِأَبِينَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّمَا قَالُوا رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen Ali<sup>asws</sup> passed by a group of people, so he<sup>asws</sup> greeted (السَّلَامُ) upon them. But rather, they said, ‘Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Blessings be upon you<sup>as</sup>, the People of the Household’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the complete welcome for the staying one (not travelling), is the handshake, and the complete greeting (السَّلَامُ) upon the traveller is the hugging’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ مِنْ تَمَامِ التَّحِيَّةِ لِلْمُقِيمِ الْمُصَافَحَةَ وَ تَمَامِ التَّسْلِيمِ عَلَى الْمُسَافِرِ الْمُعَانَقَةَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the complete welcome for the staying one (not travelling), is the handshake, and the complete greeting (السَّلَامُ) upon the traveller is the hugging’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: سكت عنه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/542)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> disliked it for the man that he should be saying, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you alive’, then he is silent, without offering the greetings of peace’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:7
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) يُكْرَهُ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَقُولَ حَيَّاكَ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ يَسْكُتَ حَتَّى يَتْبَعَهَا بِالسَّلَامِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> disliked it for the man that he should be saying, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you alive’, then he is silent, without offering the greetings of peace’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: سكت عنه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/542)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The younger one should offer the greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the older, and the passer-by upon the seated one, and the few upon the more’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:8
citation.arabic_text: يُسَلِّمُ الصَّغِيرُ عَلَى الْكَبِيرِ وَ الْمَارُّ عَلَى الْقَاعِدِ وَ الْقَلِيلُ عَلَى الْكَثِيرِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The younger one should offer the greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the older, and the passer-by upon the seated one, and the few upon the more’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/543)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Anbasa Bin Mus’ab, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The few would be initiating the more with the greeting (السَّلَامُ), and the rider would initiate the walker, and the owner (rider) of the mules would initiate the owner (rider) of the donkeys, and the owner (rider) of the cavalry horse would be initiating the owner (rider) of the mules’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:8
citation.arabic_text: الْقَلِيلُ يَبْدَءُونَ الْكَثِيرَ بِالسَّلَامِ وَ الرَّاكِبُ يَبْدَأُ الْمَاشِيَ وَ أَصْحَابُ الْبِغَالِ يَبْدَءُونَ أَصْحَابَ الْحَمِيرِ وَ أَصْحَابُ الْخَيْلِ يَبْدَءُونَ أَصْحَابَ الْبِغَالِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Anbasa Bin Mus’ab, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The few would be initiating the more with the greeting (السَّلَامُ), and the rider would initiate the walker, and the owner (rider) of the mules would initiate the owner (rider) of the donkeys, and the owner (rider) of the cavalry horse would be initiating the owner (rider) of the mules’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/543)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The rider should greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the walker, and the walker upon the seated one; and whenever a group meets a group, the few should greet upon the more; and when one (person) meets a group, the one should greet upon the group’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:8
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ يُسَلِّمُ الرَّاكِبُ عَلَى الْمَاشِي وَ الْمَاشِي عَلَى الْقَاعِدِ وَ إِذَا لَقِيَتْ جَمَاعَةٌ جَمَاعَةً سَلَّمَ الْأَقَلُّ عَلَى الْأَكْثَرِ وَ إِذَا لَقِيَ وَاحِدٌ جَمَاعَةً سَلَّمَ الْوَاحِدُ عَلَى الْجَمَاعَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The rider should greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the walker, and the walker upon the seated one; and whenever a group meets a group, the few should greet upon the more; and when one (person) meets a group, the one should greet upon the group’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/543)

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The rider should greet the walker, and the standing one upon the seated one’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:8
citation.arabic_text: يُسَلِّمُ الرَّاكِبُ عَلَى الْمَاشِي وَ الْقَائِمُ عَلَى الْقَاعِدِ .
citation.translation: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The rider should greet the walker, and the standing one upon the seated one’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/543)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Jameel, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When a group enters into a gathering, then (another) group proceeds and enters, so it is upon the ones entering later, when they do enter, that they should greet (السَّلَامُ) upon them (the first one)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:8
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا كَانَ قَوْمٌ فِي مَجْلِسٍ ثُمَّ سَبَقَ قَوْمٌ فَدَخَلُوا فَعَلَى الدَّاخِلِ أَخِيراً إِذَا دَخَلَ أَنْ يُسَلِّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Jameel, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When a group enters into a gathering, then (another) group proceeds and enters, so it is upon the ones entering later, when they do enter, that they should greet (السَّلَامُ) upon them (the first one)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/543)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever a group passes by a group of people, it would suffice for them if one of them was to greet (السَّلَامُ); and when a group is greeted upon, and they are a group, it would suffice them if one of them was to respond’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:9
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا مَرَّتِ الْجَمَاعَةُ بِقَوْمٍ أَجْزَأَهُمْ أَنْ يُسَلِّمَ وَاحِدٌ مِنْهُمْ وَ إِذَا سَلَّمَ عَلَى الْقَوْمِ وَ هُمْ جَمَاعَةٌ أَجْزَأَهُمْ أَنْ يَرُدَّ وَاحِدٌ مِنْهُمْ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever a group passes by a group of people, it would suffice for them if one of them was to greet (السَّلَامُ); and when a group is greeted upon, and they are a group, it would suffice them if one of them was to respond’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/544)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the man from a group greets (السَّلَامُ), it would suffice (all of) them’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:9
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا سَلَّمَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ الْجَمَاعَةِ أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُمْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the man from a group greets (السَّلَامُ), it would suffice (all of) them’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/544)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When one from a group greets (السَّلَامُ), it would suffice from (all of) them, and when one responds, it would suffice from (all of) them’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:9
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا سَلَّمَ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ وَاحِدٌ أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُمْ وَ إِذَا رَدَّ وَاحِدٌ أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُمْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When one from a group greets (السَّلَامُ), it would suffice from (all of) them, and when one responds, it would suffice from (all of) them’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/544)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabi’e Bin Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It was so that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the women and they were returning the greeting upon him<sup>saww</sup>; and it was so that Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> would greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the women, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to dislike greeting (السَّلَامُ) upon the young ones from them, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying (it is so that): ‘One should be afraid that her voice might astound him, so what would enter upon him would be more than what he is seeking from the Recompense’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:10
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يُسَلِّمُ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ وَ يَرْدُدْنَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامَ وَ كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) يُسَلِّمُ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ وَ كَانَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يُسَلِّمَ عَلَى الشَّابَّةِ مِنْهُنَّ وَ يَقُولُ أَتَخَوَّفُ أَنْ يُعْجِبَنِي صَوْتُهَا فَيَدْخُلَ عَلَيَّ أَكْثَرُ مِمَّا أَطْلُبُ مِنَ الْأَجْرِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabi’e Bin Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It was so that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the women and they were returning the greeting upon him<sup>saww</sup>; and it was so that Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> would greet (السَّلَامُ) upon the women, and he<sup>asws</sup> used to dislike greeting (السَّلَامُ) upon the young ones from them, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying (it is so that): ‘One should be afraid that her voice might astound him, so what would enter upon him would be more than what he is seeking from the Recompense’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/545)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from IbnAzina, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘A Jew came over to Rasool-Allahsaww, and Ayesha was in hissaww presence. So he said, ‘Al-Saam Alaykum!’ (The poison be upon you). So Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Upon you (as well)’. Then another (Jew) came over and said similar to that. So hesaww replied to him just as hesaww has replied upon his companion. Then another came over, and he said similar to that’. So Rasool-Allahsaww replied just as hesaww had replied upon his two companions. So Ayesha got angered and she said, ‘And upon you be the posion, and the Wrath, and the Curse, O community of the Jews, O brethren of the monkeys and the pigs!’. So Rasool-Allahsaww said to her: ‘O Ayesha! If there was a resemblance of the obscenity, it would have been an evil resemblance. The kindness is not placed upon anything at all except that it would adorn it, and it would not be raised from it at all except that it would dishonour it’. She said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! Did yousaww not listen to their speech, ‘The poison be upon you!?’ So hesaww said: ‘Yes, Isaww did. But, did you not listen to what Isaww replied upon them? Isaww said: ‘Upon you (as well)’. So, whenever a Muslim greets upon you, so be saying, ‘Salaam Alaykum’, and when a disbeliever greets upon you, so be saying, ‘Alayka’ (the same Upon you)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:11
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلَ يَهُودِيٌّ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ عَائِشَةُ عِنْدَهُ فَقَالَ السَّامُ عَلَيْكُمْ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَلَيْكُمْ ثُمَّ دَخَلَ آخَرُ فَقَالَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ فَرَدَّ عَلَيْهِ كَمَا رَدَّ عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ ثُمَّ دَخَلَ آخَرُ فَقَالَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ فَرَدَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَمَا رَدَّ عَلَى صَاحِبَيْهِ فَغَضِبَتْ عَائِشَةُ فَقَالَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ السَّامُ وَ الْغَضَبُ وَ اللَّعْنَةُ يَا مَعْشَرَ الْيَهُودِ يَا إِخْوَةَ الْقِرَدَةِ وَ الْخَنَازِيرِ فَقَالَ لَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَا عَائِشَةُ إِنَّ الْفُحْشَ لَوْ كَانَ مُمَثَّلًا لَكَانَ مِثَالَ سَوْءٍ إِنَّ الرِّفْقَ لَمْ يُوضَعْ عَلَى شَيْ‏ءٍ قَطُّ إِلَّا زَانَهُ وَ لَمْ يُرْفَعْ عَنْهُ قَطُّ إِلَّا شَانَهُ قَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَ مَا سَمِعْتَ إِلَى قَوْلِهِمْ السَّامُ عَلَيْكُمْ فَقَالَ بَلَى أَ مَا سَمِعْتِ مَا رَدَدْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ قُلْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ فَإِذَا سَلَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ مُسْلِمٌ فَقُولُوا سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ إِذَا سَلَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ كَافِرٌ فَقُولُوا عَلَيْكَ .

So hesaww replied to him just as hesaww has replied upon his companion. Then another came over, and he said similar to that’. So Rasool-Allahsaww replied just as hesaww had replied upon his two companions. So Ayesha got angered and she said, ‘And upon you be the posion, and the Wrath, and the Curse, O community of the Jews, O brethren of the monkeys and the pigs!’. So Rasool-Allahsaww said to her: ‘O Ayesha! If there was a resemblance of the obscenity, it would have been an evil resemblance. The kindness is not placed upon anything at all except that it would adorn it, and it would not be raised from it at all except that it would dishonour it’. She said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! Did yousaww not listen to their speech, ‘The poison be upon you!?’ So hesaww said: ‘Yes, Isaww did. But, did you not listen to what Isaww replied upon them? Isaww said: ‘Upon you (as well)’. So, whenever a Muslim greets upon you, so be saying, ‘Salaam Alaykum’, and when a disbeliever greets upon you, so be saying, ‘Alayka’ (the same Upon you)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/545)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammd Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Do not initiate the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) with the greeting (السَّلَامُ); and when they greet upon you, so (you should) be saying, ‘Wa Alaykum’ (And upon you)’.

citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammd Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Do not initiate the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) with the greeting (السَّلَامُ); and when they greet upon you, so (you should) be saying, ‘Wa Alaykum’ (And upon you)’.

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Abu Jahl Bin Hisham, and with him were a group from Qureysh, came over to Abu Talibas, and they said, ‘The sonsaww of youras brotheras has harmed us and harmed our gods, therefore instruct himas to restrain from our gods, and we would restrain from hissaww Godazwj’. So Abu Talibas sent a message to Rasool-Allahsaww, to call himsaww over. So when the Prophetsaww came over, hesaww did not see in the room except for the Polytheists. So hesaww said: ‘Greetings be upon the one who follows the Guidance!’. Then hesaww was seated. So Abu Talibas informed himsaww with what (proposal) they had come over with to himas. So hesaww said: ‘Or shall Isaww give a solution for them in a statement (There is no god except Allahazwj), which is good for them, by which they would be prevailing upon the Arabs and treading on their necks?’ So Abu Jahl said, ‘Yes, and what is this statement?’ So hesaww said: ‘You should be saying, ‘There is no god except Allahazwj’’. Heasws said: ‘So they placed their fingers in their ears and went out fleeing, and they were saying, ‘We were not made to hear this in the former nations. This is nothing except for a fabrication’. So Allahazwj the Exalted Revealed regarding their words [38:1] Saad. I Swear by the Quran, full of Remembrance – up to Hisazwj Words [38:7] this is nothing but a fabrication’.

citation.arabic_text: أَقْبَلَ أَبُو جَهْلِ بْنُ هِشَامٍ وَ مَعَهُ قَوْمٌ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ فَدَخَلُوا عَلَى أَبِي طَالِبٍ فَقَالُوا إِنَّ ابْنَ أَخِيكَ قَدْ آذَانَا وَ آذَى آلِهَتَنَا فَادْعُهُ وَ مُرْهُ فَلْيَكُفَّ عَنْ آلِهَتِنَا وَ نَكُفُّ عَنْ إِلَهِهِ قَالَ فَبَعَثَ أَبُو طَالِبٍ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَدَعَاهُ فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَمْ يَرَ فِي الْبَيْتِ إِلَّا مُشْرِكاً فَقَالَ السَّلَامُ عَلَى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدَى ثُمَّ جَلَسَ فَخَبَّرَهُ أَبُو طَالِبٍ بِمَا جَاءُوا لَهُ فَقَالَ أَ وَ هَلْ لَهُمْ فِي كَلِمَةٍ خَيْرٍ لَهُمْ مِنْ هَذَا يَسُودُونَ بِهَا الْعَرَبَ وَ يَطَئُونَ أَعْنَاقَهُمْ فَقَالَ أَبُو جَهْلٍ نَعَمْ وَ مَا هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ فَقَالَ تَقُولُونَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ قَالَ فَوَضَعُوا أَصَابِعَهُمْ فِي آذَانِهِمْ وَ خَرَجُوا هُرَّاباً وَ هُمْ يَقُولُونَ ما سَمِعْنا بِهذا فِي الْمِلَّةِ الْآخِرَةِ إِنْ هذا إِلَّا اخْتِلاقٌ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي قَوْلِهِمْ ص وَ الْقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ إِلَّا اخْتِلاقٌ .

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Kufy, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the man who happened to have the need for him to the Magian, or to the Jew, or to the Christian, or if he happens to be an office bearer or a manager of the great people of his land. So the man has to write to him regarding the need. Should he begin by his request and greet upon him in his letter, and rather he is doing that, so that perhaps he would fulfil his need?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for beginning with it, so no, but you can greet upon him in your letter, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had written to Chosroe (of Persia) and Caesar (of Rome)’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Safwan Bin Yahya who said, ‘I was in the presence of Al-Rezaasws, so heasws sneezed. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/553)

text: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said, ‘I heard Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The yawning is from the Satan<sup>la</sup> and the sneeze is from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ التَّثَاؤُبُ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ وَ الْعَطْسَةُ مِنَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said, ‘I heard Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The yawning is from the Satan<sup>la</sup> and the sneeze is from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/554)

text: Ali bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad who said, ‘I asked the knowledgeable one<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> about the sneezing and what is the reason in (saying), ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’, upon it. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘For Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> has Favoured upon His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> servant regarding the health in his body and safety of his body parts, and the servant tends to forget the Mention of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic upon that; and when he does forget, Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Commands the wind, so it goes through his body, then exits from his nose, so he Praises Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> upon that, and that praise of his during that would happen to be a thankfulness to what he had forgotten’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ الْعَالِمَ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْعَطْسَةِ وَ مَا الْعِلَّةُ فِي الْحَمْدِ لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهَا فَقَالَ إِنَّ لِلَّهِ نِعَماً عَلَى عَبْدِهِ فِي صِحَّةِ بَدَنِهِ وَ سَلَامَةِ جَوَارِحِهِ وَ إِنَّ الْعَبْدَ يَنْسَى ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَ إِذَا نَسِيَ أَمَرَ اللَّهُ الرِّيحَ فَتَجَاوَزَ فِي بَدَنِهِ ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُهَا مِنْ أَنْفِهِ فَيَحْمَدُ اللَّهَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ فَيَكُونُ حَمْدُهُ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ شُكْراً لِمَا نَسِيَ .
citation.translation: Ali bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad who said, ‘I asked the knowledgeable one<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> about the sneezing and what is the reason in (saying), ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’, upon it. text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ja’far Bin Yunus, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn who said, ‘We were in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, and I counted in the room, there were fourteen men. So Abu Abdullahasws sneezed, and no one from the group spoke (a word)’. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Are you not Naming (Allahazwj)? Are you not Naming (Allahazwj)? From the rights of the Momin upon the Momin is that when he is sick, that you should visit him, and when he dies, that you should attend his funeral, and when he sneezes, that you should Name (Allahazwj)’. Or heasws said: ‘Yushammituhu’ (be glad for him)’, ‘And when he invites you, that you answer him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15
citation.arabic_text: كُنَّا عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَحْصَيْتُ فِي الْبَيْتِ أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ رَجُلًا فَعَطَسَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَمَا تَكَلَّمَ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَ لَا تُسَمِّتُونَ أَ لَا تُسَمِّتُونَ مِنْ حَقِّ الْمُؤْمِنِ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِ إِذَا مَرِضَ أَنْ يَعُودَهُ وَ إِذَا مَاتَ أَنْ يَشْهَدَ جَنَازَتَهُ وَ إِذَا عَطَسَ أَنْ يُسَمِّتَهُ أَوْ قَالَ يُشَمِّتَهُ وَ إِذَا دَعَاهُ أَنْ يُجِيبَهُ .

text: Abu Ali Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The sneezing is a good thing. It is beneficial for the body, and reminds you of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’. I said, ‘In our presence there is a group of people who are saying, ‘There is no share for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> in the sneezing’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If they were lying, so may they not attain the intercession of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) نِعْمَ الشَّيْ‏ءُ الْعَطْسَةُ تَنْفَعُ فِي الْجَسَدِ وَ تُذَكِّرُ بِاللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ قُلْتُ إِنَّ عِنْدَنَا قَوْماً يَقُولُونَ لَيْسَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فِي الْعَطْسَةِ نَصِيبٌ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانُوا كَاذِبِينَ فَلَا نَالَهُمْ شَفَاعَةُ مُحَمَّدٍ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The sneezing is a good thing. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If they were lying, so may they not attain the intercession of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/555)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions who said, ‘A man sneezed in the presence of Abu Ja’farasws, so he said, ‘The Praise is for Allahazwj’, so Abu Ja’farasws did not respond (Allahazwj) and said: ‘You have been deficient of ourasws rights’. Then heasws said: ‘Whenever one of you sneezes, so let him say, ‘The Praise is for Allahazwj, Lordazwj of the worlds, and may Allahazwj Send Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, and the Peopleasws of hissaww Household’. So the man said it, and Abu Ja’farasws responded (by Naming Allahazwj)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15
citation.arabic_text: عَطَسَ رَجُلٌ عِنْدَ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ فَلَمْ يُسَمِّتْهُ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَالَ نَقَصَنَا حَقَّنَا ثُمَّ قَالَ إِذَا عَطَسَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ قَالَ فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ فَسَمَّتَهُ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions who said, ‘A man sneezed in the presence of Abu Ja’farasws, so he said, ‘The Praise is for Allahazwj’, so Abu Ja’farasws did not respond (Allahazwj) and said: ‘You have been deficient of ourasws rights’. Then heasws said: ‘Whenever one of you sneezes, so let him say, ‘The Praise is for Allahazwj, Lordazwj of the worlds, and may Allahazwj Send Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, and the Peopleasws of hissaww Household’. So the man said it, and Abu Ja’farasws responded (by Naming Allahazwj)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/555)

text: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ismail Al Basry, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘The people are disliking the (sending of) Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and hisazwj Progenyasws in three places – during the sneezing, and during the slaughtering, and during the copulation’. So Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘What is matter with them? Woe be unto them! They have become hypocrites, may Allahazwj Curse them!’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ النَّاسَ يَكْرَهُونَ الصَّلَاةَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِهِ فِي ثَلَاثَةِ مَوَاطِنَ عِنْدَ الْعَطْسَةِ وَ عِنْدَ الذَّبِيحَةِ وَ عِنْدَ الْجِمَاعِ فَقَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) مَا لَهُمْ وَيْلَهُمْ نَافَقُوا لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ .
citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ismail Al Basry, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘The people are disliking the (sending of) Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and hisazwj Progenyasws in three places – during the sneezing, and during the slaughtering, and during the copulation’. So Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘What is matter with them? Woe be unto them! They have become hypocrites, may Allahazwj Curse them!’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/555)

text: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Sa’ad Bin Abu Khalaf who said, ‘It was so that whenever Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> sneezed, so it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you<sup>asws</sup>’. citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا عَطَسَ فَقِيلَ لَهُ يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ قَالَ يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَ يَرْحَمُكُمْ وَ إِذَا عَطَسَ عِنْدَهُ إِنْسَانٌ قَالَ يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .

text: From him, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, or someone else, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘A boy who had yet to reach puberty, sneezed in the presence of the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, and he said, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’. citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15

So the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said to him: ‘May Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Place Blessings in you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/556)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Whenever a man sneezes, so let one say, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds, there being no associate for Him<sup>azwj</sup>’ and when the man Names (Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in response to the sneeze), so let him say, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you’; and when he responds, so let him say, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Forgive you and us’, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was asked about a Verse or something wherein was a Mention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Everywhere Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Mentioned therein, so it is excellent’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15

So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Everywhere Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Mentioned therein, so it is excellent’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/556)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al Husayn Bin Nuaym, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik who said, ‘Once Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> sneezed, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds’, then made his<sup>asws</sup> fingers to be upon his nose, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> rub my<sup>asws</sup> nose for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, a humble rubbing’.

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/556)

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) مَنْ قَالَ إِذَا عَطَسَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ لَمْ يَجِدْ وَجَعَ الْأُذُنَيْنِ وَ الْأَضْرَاسِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who says when he sneezes, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds, upon every state’, would not find pain of the ears and the teeth, (ever)’.

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abu Najran, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A Christian man sneezed in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. citation.arabic_text: عَطَسَ رَجُلٌ نَصْرَانِيٌّ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ لَهُ الْقَوْمُ هَدَاكَ اللَّهُ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقُولُوا يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ فَقَالُوا لَهُ إِنَّهُ نَصْرَانِيٌّ فَقَالَ لَا يَهْدِيهِ اللَّهُ حَتَّى يَرْحَمَهُ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadawa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When the Muslim man sneezes, then is silent due to an illness which happens to be with him, the Angels say on his behalf: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds’. So if he does say, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds’, then Angels would say: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Forgive (your sins) for you’’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘A sneeze of the sick one is evidence of the well-being and the rest for the body’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Yaqoub Bi Yazeed, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdul Samad Bin Bashir, from Huzeyfa Bin Mansour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A sneeze is beneficial in the body, all of it, for as long as it does not increase upon the three (sneezes). So when it does exceed upon the three, so it is an illness and a disease’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ الْعُطَاسُ يَنْفَعُ فِي الْبَدَنِ كُلِّهِ مَا لَمْ يَزِدْ عَلَى الثَّلَاثِ فَإِذَا زَادَ عَلَى الثَّلَاثِ فَهُوَ دَاءٌ وَ سُقْمٌ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Yaqoub Bi Yazeed, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdul Samad Bin Bashir, from Huzeyfa Bin Mansour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A sneeze is beneficial in the body, all of it, for as long as it does not increase upon the three (sneezes). text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Kufy, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [31:19] surely the most hateful of voices is the voice of the donkeys. Heasws said: ‘The ugly sneezing’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who sneezes, then places his hand upon a nostril of his nose, then says, ‘The Praise is for Allahazwj, Lordazwj of the worlds, abundant Praise just as Heazwj is Rightful of it, and Salawāt of Allahazwj be upon Muhammadsaww the Prophetsaww and hissaww Progenyasws, and greetings’, there would come out from his left nostril, a bird smaller than the locust, and larger than the fly, until it travels to be beneath the Throne, seeking Forgiveness of Allahazwj for him up to the Day of Judgment’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ عَطَسَ ثُمَّ وَضَعَ يَدَهُ عَلَى قَصَبَةِ أَنْفِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ حَمْداً كَثِيراً كَمَا هُوَ أَهْلُهُ وَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ النَّبِيِّ وَ آلِهِ وَ سَلَّمَ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَنْخِرِهِ الْأَيْسَرِ طَائِرٌ أَصْغَرُ مِنَ الْجَرَادِ وَ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الذُّبَابِ حَتَّى يَسِيرَ تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ يَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لَهُ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who sneezes, then places his hand upon a nostril of his nose, then says, ‘The Praise is for Allahazwj, Lordazwj of the worlds, abundant Praise just as Heazwj is Rightful of it, and Salawāt of Allahazwj be upon Muhammadsaww the Prophetsaww and hissaww Progenyasws, and greetings’, there would come out from his left nostril, a bird smaller than the locust, and larger than the fly, until it travels to be beneath the Throne, seeking Forgiveness of Allahazwj for him up to the Day of Judgment’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, reporting it from a man from the general Muslims having said, ‘I used to sit in a gathering of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I had not seen a gathering nobler than his<sup>asws</sup> gathering. He<sup>asws</sup> said to me one day, ‘From where does the sneeze come out?’ So I said, ‘From the nose’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘You are wrong’. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! From where does it come out?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the entire body, just as the sperm comes out from the entire body, and its exit is from the urethra’. Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Have you not seen the person when he sneezes, his body parts shake? And the sneezer is safe from the death for seven days’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:15
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا عَطَسَ الرَّجُلُ ثَلَاثاً فَسَمِّتْهُ ثُمَّ اتْرُكْهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhassin Bin Ahmad, from Aban Bin usman, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When a man sneezes three (times), so Name (Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in response) and leave him (if he sneezes any more)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/559)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘From the Respect of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is respecting an aged old man’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:16
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ مِنْ إِجْلَالِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِجْلَالَ الشَّيْخِ الْكَبِيرِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘From the Respect of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is respecting an aged old man’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ عَرَفَ فَضْلَ كَبِيرٍ لِسِنِّهِ فَوَقَّرَهُ آمَنَهُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَزَعِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ .

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:16
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ وَقَّرَ ذَا شَيْبَةٍ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ آمَنَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مِنْ فَزَعِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/560)

text: A number of our companions,from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Khattab narrating from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (people), none would ignore their rights except for a hypocrite well-known with the hypocrisy – one with old age in Al-Islam, and a bearer (memoriser) of the Quran, and the just Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:16
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْخَطَّابِ يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ ثَلَاثَةٌ لَا يَجْهَلُ حَقَّهُمْ إِلَّا مُنَافِقٌ مَعْرُوفٌ بِالنِّفَاقِ ذُو الشَّيْبَةِ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ وَ حَامِلُ الْقُرْآنِ وَ الْإِمَامُ الْعَادِلُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions,from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Khattab narrating from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (people), none would ignore their rights except for a hypocrite well-known with the hypocrisy – one with old age in Al-Islam, and a bearer (memoriser) of the Quran, and the just Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: سكت عنه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/560)

text: From him, from his father, from Abu Nahshal, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘From the respect of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is respecting the Momin with old age; and the one who honours a Momin, so he has begun by honouring Allahazwj, and the one takes lightly with a Momin with old age, Allahazwj would Send him one who would take lightly with him before his death’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:16
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مِنْ إِجْلَالِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِجْلَالُ الْمُؤْمِنِ ذِي الشَّيْبَةِ وَ مَنْ أَكْرَمَ مُؤْمِناً فَبِكَرَامَةِ اللَّهِ بَدَأَ وَ مَنِ اسْتَخَفَّ بِمُؤْمِنٍ ذِي شَيْبَةٍ أَرْسَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ مَنْ يَسْتَخِفُّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Abu Nahshal, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘From the respect of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is respecting the Momin with old age; and the one who honours a Momin, so he has begun by honouring Allahazwj, and the one takes lightly with a Momin with old age, Allahazwj would Send him one who would take lightly with him before his death’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: سكت عنه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/560)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’adan Bin Muslim, from Abu Baseer, and someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the respect of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is the respect for the Muslim with an old age’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:16
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ مِنْ إِجْلَالِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِجْلَالُ ذِي الشَّيْبَةِ الْمُسْلِمِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’adan Bin Muslim, from Abu Baseer, and someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the respect of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is the respect for the Muslim with an old age’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: سكت عنه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/560)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Two men came over to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> placed a pillow for each one of them, and one of them sat upon it and the other one refused. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Sit upon it, for no one refuses an honouring except for a donkey’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When an honourable one of a people comes over to you, so honour him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:17
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلَ رَجُلَانِ عَلَى أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فَأَلْقَى لِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا وِسَادَةً فَقَعَدَ عَلَيْهَا أَحَدُهُمَا وَ أَبَى الْآخَرُ فَقَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) اقْعُدْ عَلَيْهَا فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَأْبَى الْكَرَامَةَ إِلَّا حِمَارٌ ثُمَّ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا أَتَاكُمْ كَرِيمُ قَوْمٍ فَأَكْرِمُوهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Two men came over to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> placed a pillow for each one of them, and one of them sat upon it and the other one refused. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Sit upon it, for no one refuses an honouring except for a donkey’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When an honourable one of a people comes over to you, so honour him’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا أَتَاكُمْ كَرِيمُ قَوْمٍ فَأَكْرِمُوهُ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Al Alawy, from his father, from his grandfather who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When Udayy Bin Hatim proceeded to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> entered him into his<sup>saww</sup> house, and there did not happen to be in the house apart from a sack and a pillow of animal skin. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> placed it for him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:17
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَمَّا قَدِمَ عَدِيُّ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَدْخَلَهُ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بَيْتَهُ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَيْرُ خَصَفَةٍ وَ وِسَادَةٍ مِنْ أَدَمٍ فَطَرَحَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِعَدِيِّ بْنِ حَاتِمٍ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Al Alawy, from his father, from his grandfather who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When Udayy Bin Hatim proceeded to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> entered him into his<sup>saww</sup> house, and there did not happen to be in the house apart from a sack and a pillow of animal skin. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> placed it for him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: سكت عنه - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/561)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘From the rights of a comer upon the people of the house is that he should walk with him, welcoming him, and when he goes out’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you enters a Muslim brother into his house, so he is the commander upon him until he goes out’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:18
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِنَّ مِنْ حَقِّ الدَّاخِلِ عَلَى أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ أَنْ يَمْشُوا مَعَهُ هُنَيْئَةً إِذَا دَخَلَ وَ إِذَا خَرَجَ وَ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا دَخَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَلَى أَخِيهِ الْمُسْلِمِ فِي بَيْتِهِ فَهُوَ أَمِيرٌ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يَخْرُجَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘From the rights of a comer upon the people of the house is that he should walk with him, welcoming him, and when he goes out’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you enters a Muslim brother into his house, so he is the commander upon him until he goes out’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/561)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Ibn Abu Awf, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The gatherings are with the confidentiality’ (in the hands of the attendants).

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:19
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ الْمَجَالِسُ بِالْأَمَانَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Ibn Abu Awf, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The gatherings are with the confidentiality’ (in the hands of the attendants).
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/562)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The gatherings are with the confidentiality’(in the hands of the attendants).

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:19
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) الْمَجَالِسُ بِالْأَمَانَةِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The gatherings are with the confidentiality’(in the hands of the attendants).
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/562)

text: A nuuumber of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The gatherings are with the confidentiality. No one must make public anything that one’s companion does not want to be made public unless it with his permission, or he is trusted and does it only for his good’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:19
citation.arabic_text: الْمَجَالِسُ بِالْأَمَانَةِ وَ لَيْسَ لِأَحَدٍ أَنْ يُحَدِّثَ بِحَدِيثٍ يَكْتُمُهُ صَاحِبُهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ ثِقَةً أَوْ ذِكْراً لَهُ بِخَيْرٍ .
citation.translation: A nuuumber of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The gatherings are with the confidentiality. No one must make public anything that one’s companion does not want to be made public unless it with his permission, or he is trusted and does it only for his good’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/562)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When there was a group of three, so two of them should not be whispering (to each other) because it saddens and hurts the feelings of the third’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:20
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا كَانَ الْقَوْمُ ثَلَاثَةً فَلَا يَتَنَاجَى مِنْهُمُ اثْنَانِ دُونَ صَاحِبِهِمَا فَإِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ مَا يَحْزُنُهُ وَ يُؤْذِيهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When there was a group of three, so two of them should not be whispering (to each other) because it saddens and hurts the feelings of the third’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/562)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said: ‘When there were three in a room, so two of them should not whisper (to each other) because it would sadden him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:20
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا كَانَ ثَلَاثَةٌ فِي بَيْتٍ فَلَا يَتَنَاجَى اثْنَانِ دُونَ صَاحِبِهِمَا فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا يَغُمُّهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said: ‘When there were three in a room, so two of them should not whisper (to each other) because it would sadden him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/562)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who displays (himself as) the speaker to him Muslim brother (cutting off) his discussion, so it is as if he has scratched his face’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:20
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ عَرَضَ لِأَخِيهِ الْمُسْلِمِ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ فِي حَدِيثِهِ فَكَأَنَّمَا خَدَشَ وَجْهَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who displays (himself as) the speaker to him Muslim brother (cutting off) his discussion, so it is as if he has scratched his face’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/563)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Nowfaly, from Abdul Azeem Bin Abdullah Bin Al Hassan Al Alawy, raising it, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘It was so that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> sat by three (postures) – the squatting, and it is that he<sup>saww</sup> raised both his<sup>saww</sup> legs (knees) and embraced them with his<sup>saww</sup> hand, and tightened his<sup>saww</sup> hands in his<sup>saww</sup> arms; and he<sup>saww</sup> used to bow upon his<sup>saww</sup> knees, and he<sup>saww</sup> would bend one leg and extend the other one upon it; and he<sup>saww</sup> was not seen cross-legged at all’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:21
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَجْلِسُ ثَلَاثاً الْقُرْفُصَا وَ هُوَ أَنْ يُقِيمَ سَاقَيْهِ وَ يَسْتَقْبِلَهُمَا بِيَدَيْهِ وَ يَشُدَّ يَدَهُ فِي ذِرَاعِهِ وَ كَانَ يَجْثُو عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْهِ وَ كَانَ يَثْنِي رِجْلًا وَاحِدَةً وَ يَبْسُطُ عَلَيْهَا الْأُخْرَى وَ لَمْ يُرَ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مُتَرَبِّعاً قَطُّ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Nowfaly, from Abdul Azeem Bin Abdullah Bin Al Hassan Al Alawy, raising it, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘It was so that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> sat by three (postures) – the squatting, and it is that he<sup>saww</sup> raised both his<sup>saww</sup> legs (knees) and embraced them with his<sup>saww</sup> hand, and tightened his<sup>saww</sup> hands in his<sup>saww</sup> arms; and he<sup>saww</sup> used to bow upon his<sup>saww</sup> knees, and he<sup>saww</sup> would bend one leg and extend the other one upon it; and he<sup>saww</sup> was not seen cross-legged at all’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول أو مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/563)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly who said, ‘I saw Ali Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> seated placing one of his<sup>asws</sup> legs upon his<sup>asws</sup> thigh. citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَكْثَرَ مَا يَجْلِسُ تُجَاهَ الْقِبْلَةِ .

text: Abu Abdullah Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws sat ‘Mutawarrika’, hisasws right leg being upon hisasws left thigh. So a man said to himasws, ‘This is an abhorrent sitting posture’. So heasws said: ‘No. But rather, it is a thing which the Jews say that when Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic was free from Creating the skies and the earth and Established upon the Throne, Sat in this posture in order to rest. So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Revealed [2:255] Allah is He besides Whom there is no god, the Everliving, the Eternal; slumber does not seize Him nor sleep, and Abu Abdullahasws remained sitting ‘Mutawarrika’ posture just as heasws was’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:21
citation.arabic_text: جَلَسَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مُتَوَرِّكاً رِجْلُهُ الْيُمْنَى عَلَى فَخِذِهِ الْيُسْرَى فَقَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ هَذِهِ جِلْسَةٌ مَكْرُوهَةٌ فَقَالَ لَا إِنَّمَا هُوَ شَيْ‏ءٌ قَالَتْهُ الْيَهُودُ لَمَّا أَنْ فَرَغَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مِنْ خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَ الْأَرْضِ وَ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ جَلَسَ هَذِهِ الْجِلْسَةَ لِيَسْتَرِيحَ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ لا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَ لا نَوْمٌ وَ بَقِيَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مُتَوَرِّكاً كَمَا هُوَ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It was so that whenever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> entered a house, he<sup>saww</sup> sat in the nearest place to him<sup>saww</sup> where he<sup>saww</sup> entered (from)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:21
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا دَخَلَ مَنْزِلًا قَعَدَ فِي أَدْنَى الْمَجْلِسِ إِلَيْهِ حِينَ يَدْخُلُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It was so that whenever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> entered a house, he<sup>saww</sup> sat in the nearest place to him<sup>saww</sup> where he<sup>saww</sup> entered (from)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/564)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Talha Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The market of the Muslims is like their Masjid. So the one who preceded to a place, so he is more rightful with it up to the night’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And it was so that he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> did not used to take rent for the market rooms (stalls)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:21
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) سُوقُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كَمَسْجِدِهِمْ فَمَنْ سَبَقَ إِلَى مَكَانٍ فَهُوَ أَحَقُّ بِهِ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ قَالَ وَ كَانَ لَا يَأْخُذُ عَلَى بُيُوتِ السُّوقِ كِرَاءً .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: كالموثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/564)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is befitting for the sitting ones during the summer that there happens to be between every two, a measurement of an arm bone (elbow’s length), lest it be grievous from some of them upon the others in the heat’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:21
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَنْبَغِي لِلْجُلَسَاءِ فِي الصَّيْفِ أَنْ يَكُونَ بَيْنَ كُلِّ اثْنَيْنِ مِقْدَارُ عَظْمِ الذِّرَاعِ لِئَلَّا يَشُقَّ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ فِي الْحَرِّ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is befitting for the sitting ones during the summer that there happens to be between every two, a measurement of an arm bone (elbow’s length), lest it be grievous from some of them upon the others in the heat’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/565)

text: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from hammad Bin Usman who said, ‘I saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> sit in his<sup>asws</sup> house by the door of his house, facing the Qiblah’.

citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from hammad Bin Usman who said, ‘I saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> sit in his<sup>asws</sup> house by the door of his house, facing the Qiblah’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/565)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The reclining in the Masjid is the monasticism of the Arabs. A Momin is such that his sitting is his Masjid (place of worship), and his monastery is his house’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:22
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) الِاتِّكَاءُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ رَهْبَانِيَّةُ الْعَرَبِ إِنَّ الْمُؤْمِنَ مَجْلِسُهُ مَسْجِدُهُ وَ صَوْمَعَتُهُ بَيْتُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The reclining in the Masjid is the monasticism of the Arabs. citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:22

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man sat cross-legged being in one (piece of) cloth. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he had covered up his private part, so there is no problem’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:22
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَحْتَبِي بِثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ يُغَطِّي عَوْرَتَهُ فَلَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man sat cross-legged being in one (piece of) cloth.
