citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/566)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is not allowed for the man that he sits cross-legged facing the Kabah’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:22
citation.arabic_text: لَا يَجُوزُ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَحْتَبِيَ مُقَابِلَ الْكَعْبَةِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is not allowed for the man that he sits cross-legged facing the Kabah’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/566)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Isa, from Moammar Bin Khallad who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The man happens to be with a group, and the speech flows between them, so they are joking and laughing’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem for as long as there does not happen to be . . .’. So I thought he<sup>asws</sup> meant the immoralities. Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘It was so that Bedouins would come to Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> and bring gifts for him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, and they was saying, ‘Give us the price of our gifts’. So Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> would laugh; and when he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> was sad he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> asked: ‘What happened to the Bedouin? If only he would come to us<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ الرَّجُلُ يَكُونُ مَعَ الْقَوْمِ فَيَجْرِي بَيْنَهُمْ كَلَامٌ يَمْزَحُونَ وَ يَضْحَكُونَ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فَظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهُ عَنَى الْفُحْشَ ثُمَّ قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَانَ يَأْتِيهِ الْأَعْرَابِيُّ فَيُهْدِي لَهُ الْهَدِيَّةَ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ مَكَانَهُ أَعْطِنَا ثَمَنَ هَدِيَّتِنَا فَيَضْحَكُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ كَانَ إِذَا اغْتَمَّ يَقُولُ مَا فَعَلَ الْأَعْرَابِيُّ لَيْتَهُ أَتَانَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Isa, from Moammar Bin Khallad who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The man happens to be with a group, and the speech flows between them, so they are joking and laughing’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem for as long as there does not happen to be . . .’. So I thought he<sup>asws</sup> meant the immoralities. Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘It was so that Bedouins would come to Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> and bring gifts for him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, and they was saying, ‘Give us the price of our gifts’. So Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> would laugh; and when he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> was sad he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> asked: ‘What happened to the Bedouin? If only he would come to us<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/567)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Shareef Bin Sabiq, from Al Fazl Bin Abu Qurra, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘There is none from a Momin except there is humour in him’. I said, ‘And what is the humour?’ Heasws said: ‘The (tales in) joyful (manners)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: مَا مِنْ مُؤْمِنٍ إِلَّا وَ فِيهِ دُعَابَةٌ قُلْتُ وَ مَا الدُّعَابَةُ قَالَ الْمِزَاحُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Shareef Bin Sabiq, from Al Fazl Bin Abu Qurra, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘There is none from a Momin except there is humour in him’. I said, ‘And what is the humour?’ Heasws said: ‘The (tales in) joyful (manners)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/567)

text: Fromhim, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Yahya Bin Sllam, from Yusuf Bin Yaqoub, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Yunus Al Shaybani who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How is the humouring of some of you unto the others?’ I said, ‘Little’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not be doing so (being of little humour), for the humour is from the good morals, and you would be entering the cheerfulness by it upon your brother, and it was so that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would humour the man intending to cheer him up’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) كَيْفَ مُدَاعَبَةُ بَعْضِكُمْ بَعْضاً قُلْتُ قَلِيلٌ قَالَ فَلَا تَفْعَلُوا فَإِنَّ الْمُدَاعَبَةَ مِنْ حُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ وَ إِنَّكَ لَتُدْخِلُ بِهَا السُّرُورَ عَلَى أَخِيكَ وَ لَقَدْ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يُدَاعِبُ الرَّجُلَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَسُرَّهُ .
citation.translation: Fromhim, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Yahya Bin Sllam, from Yusuf Bin Yaqoub, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Yunus Al Shaybani who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How is the humouring of some of you unto the others?’ I said, ‘Little’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not be doing so (being of little humour), for the humour is from the good morals, and you would be entering the cheerfulness by it upon your brother, and it was so that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would humour the man intending to cheer him up’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/567)

text: Salih Bin Uqba, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Ju’fy who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Loves the humour (taking place) in the group without there being any obscenities’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يُحِبُّ الْمُدَاعِبَ فِي الْجَمَاعَةِ بِلَا رَفَثٍ .
citation.translation: Salih Bin Uqba, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Ju’fy who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Loves the humour (taking place) in the group without there being any obscenities’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/567)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Al hassan Bin Kuleyb, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The laughter of the Momin is a smile’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: ضَحِكُ الْمُؤْمِنِ تَبَسُّمٌ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Al hassan Bin Kuleyb, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The laughter of the Momin is a smile’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/568)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour, from Hareyz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Abundant laughter deadens the heart’. And he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Abundant laughter dissolves the Religion just as the water dissolves the salt’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: كَثْرَةُ الضَّحِكِ تُمِيتُ الْقَلْبَ وَ قَالَ كَثْرَةُ الضَّحِكِ تَمِيثُ الدِّينَ كَمَا يَمِيثُ الْمَاءُ الْمِلْحَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour, from Hareyz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Abundant laughter deadens the heart’. And he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Abundant laughter dissolves the Religion just as the water dissolves the salt’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/568)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the ignorance is the laughter from without any wonderment’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Do not manifest your teeth from a laughter and you have committed the disgraceful deeds, and there is no security overnight from the evil deeds’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ مِنَ الْجَهْلِ الضَّحِكَ مِنْ غَيْرِ عَجَبٍ قَالَ وَ كَانَ يَقُولُ لَا تُبْدِيَنَّ عَنْ وَاضِحَةٍ وَ قَدْ عَمِلْتَ الْأَعْمَالَ الْفَاضِحَةَ وَ لَا يَأْمَنِ الْبَيَاتَ مَنْ عَمِلَ السَّيِّئَاتِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘From the ignorance is the laughter from without any wonderment’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Do not manifest your teeth from a laughter and you have committed the disgraceful deeds, and there is no security overnight from the evil deeds’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/568)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Beware of the joking, for it removes with the water (dignity) of the face’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِيَّاكُمْ وَ الْمِزَاحَ فَإِنَّهُ يَذْهَبُ بِمَاءِ الْوَجْهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Beware of the joking, for it removes with the water (dignity) of the face’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/568)

text: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who narrated it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When you love a man, so neither joke with him nor argue bitterly with him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا أَحْبَبْتَ رَجُلًا فَلَا تُمَازِحْهُ وَ لَا تُمَارِهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who narrated it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When you love a man, so neither joke with him nor argue bitterly with him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/568)

text: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The guffaw (loud bursts of laughter) is from the Satan<sup>la</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: الْقَهْقَهَةُ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The guffaw (loud bursts of laughter) is from the Satan<sup>la</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/568)

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Kindy, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Anbasa Al Aabid who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Frequent laughter removes the water (dignity) of the face’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ كَثْرَةُ الضَّحِكِ تَذْهَبُ بِمَاءِ الْوَجْهِ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Kindy, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Anbasa Al Aabid who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Frequent laughter removes the water (dignity) of the face’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/569)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from IbnAl Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Beware of the joking for it would (cause) the grudges to flow, and would inherit the hatred, and it is the small insult’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِيَّاكُمْ وَ الْمِزَاحَ فَإِنَّهُ يَجُرُّ السَّخِيمَةَ وَ يُورِثُ الضَّغِينَةَ وَ هُوَ السَّبُّ الْأَصْغَرُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from IbnAl Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Beware of the joking for it would (cause) the grudges to flow, and would inherit the hatred, and it is the small insult’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Khalid Bin Tahmaan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When you guffaw (loud bursts of laughter), so say when you are free (from it), ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Do not Detest me’’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا قَهْقَهْتَ فَقُلْ حِينَ تَفْرُغُ اللَّهُمَّ لَا تَمْقُتْنِي .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Khalid Bin Tahmaan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When you guffaw (loud bursts of laughter), so say when you are free (from it), ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Do not Detest me’’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/569)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hajjal, from Dawood Bin Farqad and Ali Bin Uqba and Sa’alba, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullahasws and Abu Ja’farasws, or one of the twoasws having said: ‘The joking removes the water (dignity) of the face, and frequent laughter hurls out the Eman with a hurling’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: كَثْرَةُ الْمِزَاحِ تَذْهَبُ بِمَاءِ الْوَجْهِ وَ كَثْرَةُ الضَّحِكِ تَمُجُّ الْإِيمَانَ مَجّاً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hajjal, from Dawood Bin Farqad and Ali Bin Uqba and Sa’alba, (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullahasws and Abu Ja’farasws, or one of the twoasws having said: ‘The joking removes the water (dignity) of the face, and frequent laughter hurls out the Eman with a hurling’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/569)

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الْمِزَاحُ السِّبَابُ الْأَصْغَرُ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Anbasa Al Aabid who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The jokes are the smaller insults’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/569)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Beware of the joking, for it does away with the water (dignity) of the face, and the sublimity of the men’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: إِيَّاكُمْ وَ الْمِزَاحَ فَإِنَّهُ يَذْهَبُ بِمَاءِ الْوَجْهِ وَ مَهَابَةِ الرِّجَالِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Beware of the joking, for it does away with the water (dignity) of the face, and the sublimity of the men’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/569)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, from Abu Al Abbas, from Ammar Bin Marwan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not dispute bitterly for it would remove your glory, nor joke, for they (others) would take liberties upon you’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تُمَارِ فَيَذْهَبَ بَهَاؤُكَ وَ لَا تُمَازِحْ فَيُجْتَرَأَ عَلَيْكَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, from Abu Al Abbas, from Ammar Bin Marwan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not dispute bitterly for it would remove your glory, nor joke, for they (others) would take liberties upon you’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/570)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Ammar Bin Marwan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not joke (with people) for they would take liberties upon you’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: لَا تُمَازِحْ فَيُجْتَرَأَ عَلَيْكَ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/570)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa’ad Bin Abu Khalaf, (It has been narrated) from Al Hassanasws having said in a bequest of hisasws to one of hisasws sons, or said: ‘Myasws fatherasws said to one of hisasws sons: ‘Beware of the joking, for it would remove the light of your Eman, and would lighten your manliness’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: فِي وَصِيَّةٍ لَهُ لِبَعْضِ وُلْدِهِ أَوْ قَالَ قَالَ أَبِي لِبَعْضِ وُلْدِهِ إِيَّاكَ وَ الْمِزَاحَ فَإِنَّهُ يَذْهَبُ بِنُورِ إِيمَانِكَ وَ يَسْتَخِفُّ بِمُرُوءَتِكَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa’ad Bin Abu Khalaf, (It has been narrated) from Al Hassanasws having said in a bequest of hisasws to one of hisasws sons, or said: ‘Myasws fatherasws said to one of hisasws sons: ‘Beware of the joking, for it would remove the light of your Eman, and would lighten your manliness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/570)

text: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jahm, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said: ‘It was so that Yahya Bin Zakariyya<sup>as</sup> would cry and not laugh, and it was so that Isa<sup>as</sup> Bin Maryam<sup>as</sup> would laugh and cry, and that which Isa<sup>as</sup> did is superior than that which was done by Yahya<sup>as</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:23
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ يَحْيَى بْنُ زَكَرِيَّا ( عليه السلام ) يَبْكِي وَ لَا يَضْحَكُ وَ كَانَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ ( عليه السلام ) يَضْحَكُ وَ يَبْكِي وَ كَانَ الَّذِي يَصْنَعُ عِيسَى ( عليه السلام ) أَفْضَلَ مِنَ الَّذِي كَانَ يَصْنَعُ يَحْيَى ( عليه السلام ) .
citation.translation: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jahm, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said: ‘It was so that Yahya Bin Zakariyya<sup>as</sup> would cry and not laugh, and it was so that Isa<sup>as</sup> Bin Maryam<sup>as</sup> would laugh and cry, and that which Isa<sup>as</sup> did is superior than that which was done by Yahya<sup>as</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/570)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umer and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Husayn Bin Is’haq, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Ali Bin Fazzal, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, altogether from Muawiya Bin Ammar, from Amro bin Ikrama who said: ‘I went over to Abu Abdullahasws, and I said to himasws, ‘There is a neighbour of mine who is bothering me’. So heasws said: ‘Be merciful to him’. So I said, ‘May Allahazwj not have Mercy on him’. So heasws turned hisasws face away from me, so I disliked leaving himasws (like this), so I said, ‘He has done such and such with me, and keeps on doing it and is bothering me’. So heasws said: ‘What is your view, if Iasws were to bring him into the open, would you turn out to be more just than him?’ So I said, ‘Yes, I would exceed (in fairness) upon him’. So heasws said: That one is from the ones who envy the people upon what Allahazwj has Given them from Hisazwj Grace. So when he sees a Bounty upon anyone, and if there was a family for him, he would be like a curse upon them, and if there does not happen to be a family for him, he would make it to be upon his servant. So if there does not happen to be a servant for him, he would stay awake during his night and be wrathful by his day. A man from the Helpers came over to Rasool-Allahsaww and he said, ‘I bought a house among the Clan of so and so, and the closest neighbour of mine to me is a neighbour from whom I do not hope for any goodness nor do I feel safe from his evil’. So Rasool-Allahsaww instructed Aliasws, and Salmanas, and Abu Zarras’, and I forgot the other one, and I think heasws mentioned Al-Miqdad’, ‘that they call out in the Masjid by the highest of their voices that, ‘There is no Eman for the one whose neighbour is not safe from him with his deeds’. So theyas called out with it three (times). Then heasws gestured by hisasws hand, ‘Up to forty houses from in front of him, and from behind him, and from his right and from his left (are all regarded as neighbours)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:24
citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لِي جَارٌ يُؤْذِينِي فَقَالَ ارْحَمْهُ فَقُلْتُ لَا رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ فَصَرَفَ وَجْهَهُ عَنِّي قَالَ فَكَرِهْتُ أَنْ أَدَعَهُ فَقُلْتُ يَفْعَلُ بِي كَذَا وَ كَذَا وَ يَفْعَلُ بِي وَ يُؤْذِينِي فَقَالَ أَ رَأَيْتَ إِنْ كَاشَفْتَهُ انْتَصَفْتَ مِنْهُ فَقُلْتُ بَلَى أُرْبِي عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ إِنَّ ذَا مِمَّنْ يَحْسُدُ النَّاسَ عَلَى مَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ فَإِذَا رَأَى نِعْمَةً عَلَى أَحَدٍ فَكَانَ لَهُ أَهْلٌ جَعَلَ بَلَاءَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ أَهْلٌ جَعَلَهُ عَلَى خَادِمِهِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ خَادِمٌ أَسْهَرَ لَيْلَهُ وَ أَغَاظَ نَهَارَهُ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْأَنْصَارِ فَقَالَ إِنِّي اشْتَرَيْتُ دَاراً فِي بَنِي فُلَانٍ وَ إِنَّ أَقْرَبَ جِيرَانِي مِنِّي جِوَاراً مَنْ لَا أَرْجُو خَيْرَهُ وَ لَا آمَنُ شَرَّهُ قَالَ فَأَمَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَلِيّاً ( عليه السلام ) وَ سَلْمَانَ وَ أَبَا ذَرٍّ وَ نَسِيتُ آخَرَ وَ أَظُنُّهُ الْمِقْدَادَ أَنْ يُنَادُوا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ بِأَعْلَى أَصْوَاتِهِمْ بِأَنَّهُ لَا إِيمَانَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَأْمَنْ جَارُهُ بَوَائِقَهُ فَنَادَوْا بِهَا ثَلَاثاً ثُمَّ أَوْمَأَ بِيَدِهِ إِلَى كُلِّ أَرْبَعِينَ دَاراً مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ وَ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ عَنْ شِمَالِهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umer and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Husayn Bin Is’haq, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Ali Bin Fazzal, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, altogether from Muawiya Bin Ammar, from Amro bin Ikrama who said: ‘I went over to Abu Abdullahasws, and I said to himasws, ‘There is a neighbour of mine who is bothering me’. So heasws said: ‘Be merciful to him’. So I said, ‘May Allahazwj not have Mercy on him’. So heasws turned hisasws face away from me, so I disliked leaving himasws (like this), so I said, ‘He has done such and such with me, and keeps on doing it and is bothering me’. So heasws said: ‘What is your view, if Iasws were to bring him into the open, would you turn out to be more just than him?’ So I said, ‘Yes, I would exceed (in fairness) upon him’. So heasws said: That one is from the ones who envy the people upon what Allahazwj has Given them from Hisazwj Grace. So when he sees a Bounty upon anyone, and if there was a family for him, he would be like a curse upon them, and if there does not happen to be a family for him, he would make it to be upon his servant. So Rasool-Allahsaww instructed Aliasws, and Salmanas, and Abu Zarras’, and I forgot the other one, and I think heasws mentioned Al-Miqdad’, ‘that they call out in the Masjid by the highest of their voices that, ‘There is no Eman for the one whose neighbour is not safe from him with his deeds’. So theyas called out with it three (times). text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Talha Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> read in the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup> that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> wrote between the Emigrants and the Helpers and the ones attached with them from the people of Yasrib: ‘The neighbour is like the soul, neither to be harmed nor sinned (against), and the sanctity of the neighbour upon the neighbour is like the sanctity of his mother’. citation.arabic_text: قَرَأْتُ فِي كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ) أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كَتَبَ بَيْنَ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَ الْأَنْصَارِ وَ مَنْ لَحِقَ بِهِمْ مِنْ أَهْلِ يَثْرِبَ أَنَّ الْجَارَ كَالنَّفْسِ غَيْرُ مُضَارٍّ وَ لَا آثِمٍ وَ حُرْمَةُ الْجَارِ عَلَى الْجَارِ كَحُرْمَةِ أُمِّهِ الْحَدِيثُ مُخْتَصَرٌ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Al Kahily who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Yaqoub<sup>asws</sup>, when Beyamin<sup>as</sup> went away from him<sup>as</sup>, called out: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! But recall the sheep which you<sup>as</sup> slaughtered it and roasted it and ate, while so and so from your<sup>as</sup> side (neighbour) Fasted, not attaining anything from it”’.

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Hanan Bin Sadeyr, (It has been narrated) from his father, from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘A man came over to Rasool-Allahsaww and complained to himsaww of the harm from his neighbour. So Rasool-Allahsaww said to him: ‘Be patient’. Then he came over to himsaww for a second time, so the Prophetsaww said to him: ‘Be patient’. Then he returned to himsaww, and he complained to himsaww for the third time. So the Prophetsaww said to the man who complained: ‘When you are in the presence of the commuting of the people to the Friday Salat, so take out your household belongings to be on the road until the one who is going to the Friday Salat would see. So when they ask you, inform them (you are escaping from the harm of your neighbour)’. Heasws said: ‘He did so, and his harming neighbour came over to him and said to him, ‘Return your belongings, as Allahazwj is for Youazwj, (and would be) against me, if I will were to repeat (harming you)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:24
citation.arabic_text: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَشَكَا إِلَيْهِ أَذًى مِنْ جَارِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) اصْبِرْ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ ثَانِيَةً فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) اصْبِرْ ثُمَّ عَادَ إِلَيْهِ فَشَكَاهُ ثَالِثَةً فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لِلرَّجُلِ الَّذِي شَكَا إِذَا كَانَ عِنْدَ رَوَاحِ النَّاسِ إِلَى الْجُمُعَةِ فَأَخْرِجْ مَتَاعَكَ إِلَى الطَّرِيقِ حَتَّى يَرَاهُ مَنْ يَرُوحُ إِلَى الْجُمُعَةِ فَإِذَا سَأَلُوكَ فَأَخْبِرْهُمْ قَالَ فَفَعَلَ فَأَتَاهُ جَارُهُ الْمُؤْذِي لَهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ رُدَّ مَتَاعَكَ فَلَكَ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ أَنْ لَا أَعُودَ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Hanan Bin Sadeyr, (It has been narrated) from his father, from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘A man came over to Rasool-Allahsaww and complained to himsaww of the harm from his neighbour. So Rasool-Allahsaww said to him: ‘Be patient’. Then he came over to himsaww for a second time, so the Prophetsaww said to him: ‘Be patient’. Then he returned to himsaww, and he complained to himsaww for the third time. So the Prophetsaww said to the man who complained: ‘When you are in the presence of the commuting of the people to the Friday Salat, so take out your household belongings to be on the road until the one who is going to the Friday Salat would see. So when they ask you, inform them (you are escaping from the harm of your neighbour)’. Heasws said: ‘He did so, and his harming neighbour came over to him and said to him, ‘Return your belongings, as Allahazwj is for Youazwj, (and would be) against me, if I will were to repeat (harming you)’.

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Abdullah Bin usman, from Abu Al Hassan Al Bajaly, from Ubeydfullah Al Wassafy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘He has not believed in me<sup>saww</sup>, the one who spends the night satiated while his neighbour is hungry’. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, from Amro bin Ikrama, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Every forty houses (its inhabitants) are neighbours, from in front of him, and from behind him, and from his right, and from his left’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) كُلُّ أَرْبَعِينَ دَاراً جِيرَانٌ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ وَ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ عَنْ شِمَالِهِ .

text: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The limit of the neighbourhood is forty houses from every side, from in front of him, and from behind him, and from his right, and from his left’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:25
citation.arabic_text: حَدُّ الْجِوَارِ أَرْبَعُونَ دَاراً مِنْ كُلِّ جَانِبٍ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ وَ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ عَنْ شِمَالِهِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ammar Bin Marwan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> advised me saying, ‘I<sup>asws</sup> advise you with (having) the fear of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the re-payment of the entrustments, and truthful narrations, and the goodly companionship to the one who accompanies you, and there is no Strength except with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:26
citation.arabic_text: أَوْصَانِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ أُوصِيكَ بِتَقْوَى اللَّهِ وَ أَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَ صِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ وَ حُسْنِ الصِّحَابَةِ لِمَنْ صَحِبْتَ وَ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who inter-mingles (with others), so if he has the capacity that his hand can happen to be the higher (more giving than receiving), then he should do so’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:26
citation.arabic_text: مَنْ خَالَطْتَ فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَكُونَ يَدُكَ الْعُلْيَا عَلَيْهِ فَافْعَلْ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, from hisasws forefathersasws that, Amir Al-Momineenasws accompanied a Zimmy man (one living under the responsibility of an Islamic government). So the Zimmy said to himasws, ‘Where are youasws intending (to go to), O servant of Allahazwj?’ So heasws said: ‘Iasws am intending (to go to) Al-Kufa’. So when the road altered for Al-Medina, Amir Al-Momineenasws altered (hisasws direction) along with him. So the Zimmy said to himasws, ‘Did youasws not announce that youasws are intending Al-Kufa?’ So heasws said to him: ‘Yes’. So the Zimmy said to himasws, ‘So youasws have left the road (to Al-Kufa)’. So heasws said to him: ‘Iasws know that’. He said, ‘So why did youasws alter along with me and youasws have known that?’ So Amir Al-Momineenasws said to him: ‘This is from the completion of the good companionship, that the man should escort his companion for a while when he separates from him; and that is how ourasws Prophetsaww has ordered us for’. So the Zimmy said to himasws, ‘Like this?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. The Zimmy said, ‘There is no doubt rather, that the one who follows himsaww, does so due to hissaww benevolent deeds. Thus, I hereby testify that I am upon yourasws Religion’. And the Zimmy returned along with Amir Al-Momineenasws. So when he recognised himasws, became a Muslim’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:26

citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Maintenance of relationships between the brethren during the saying (not travelling) is the visitations, and during the journey, is the correspondence’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/577)

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Returning an answer to a letter is as Obligatory as the Obligation of returning the greeting, and the initiator of the greeting is closer with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:27
citation.arabic_text: رَدُّ جَوَابِ الْكِتَابِ وَاجِبٌ كَوُجُوبِ رَدِّ السَّلَامِ وَ الْبَادِي بِالسَّلَامِ أَوْلَى بِاللَّهِ وَ رَسُولِهِ .
citation.translation: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Returning an answer to a letter is as Obligatory as the Obligation of returning the greeting, and the initiator of the greeting is closer with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/577)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Jameel Bin Darraj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It was so that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to apportion his<sup>saww</sup> moments (time) between his<sup>saww</sup> companions. So he<sup>saww</sup> would look at that one, and he<sup>saww</sup> would look at that one, with the fairness’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not extend his<sup>asws</sup> legs in between his<sup>saww</sup> companions at all, and if the man was to shake his<sup>saww</sup> hand, so Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would not leave his hand from his<sup>saww</sup> hand until it so happened that he was the leaver. So when they (the people) discerned that, it was so that the man, whenever he shook his<sup>saww</sup> hand, said so with his hands, so he removed it (quickly) from his<sup>saww</sup> hand’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:28
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَقْسِمُ لَحَظَاتِهِ بَيْنَ أَصْحَابِهِ فَيَنْظُرُ إِلَى ذَا وَ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى ذَا بِالسَّوِيَّةِ قَالَ وَ لَمْ يَبْسُطْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) رِجْلَيْهِ بَيْنَ أَصْحَابِهِ قَطُّ وَ إِنْ كَانَ لَيُصَافِحُهُ الرَّجُلُ فَمَا يَتْرُكُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَدَهُ مِنْ يَدِهِ حَتَّى يَكُونَ هُوَ التَّارِكَ فَلَمَّا فَطَنُوا لِذَلِكَ كَانَ الرَّجُلُ إِذَا صَافَحَهُ قَالَ بِيَدِهِ فَنَزَعَهَا مِنْ يَدِهِ .

So when they (the people) discerned that, it was so that the man, whenever he shook his<sup>saww</sup> hand, said so with his hands, so he removed it (quickly) from his<sup>saww</sup> hand’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moammar Bin Khallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the man was present, so teknonym him, and when he was absent, so name him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:28
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا كَانَ الرَّجُلُ حَاضِراً فَكَنِّهِ وَ إِذَا كَانَ غَائِباً فَسَمِّهِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moammar Bin Khallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the man was present, so teknonym him, and when he was absent, so name him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/578)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When one of you loves his Muslim brother, so let him ask him of his name, and the name of his father, and the name of his tribe and his clan, for it is from his Obligatory rights and truthful brotherhood that he asks him about that, or else it would be a foolish recognition’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:28
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا أَحَبَّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَخَاهُ الْمُسْلِمَ فَلْيَسْأَلْهُ عَنِ اسْمِهِ وَ اسْمِ أَبِيهِ وَ اسْمِ قَبِيلَتِهِ وَ عَشِيرَتِهِ فَإِنَّ مِنْ حَقِّهِ الْوَاجِبِ وَ صِدْقِ الْإِخَاءِ أَنْ يَسْأَلَهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ وَ إِلَّا فَإِنَّهَا مَعْرِفَةُ حُمْقٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When one of you loves his Muslim brother, so let him ask him of his name, and the name of his father, and the name of his tribe and his clan, for it is from his Obligatory rights and truthful brotherhood that he asks him about that, or else it would be a foolish recognition’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/578)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ali Bin Ja’far, from Abdul Malik Bin Qudama, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘One day Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to his<sup>saww</sup> gathered ones: ‘Do you know what is (one’s) weakness?’ They said, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> are more knowing’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The weakness is of three (types) – One of you hastens to prepare food for his companion, but he breaks his promise and does not come to him (to eat food); and the second is that the man from you accompanies the man, or sits with him, loving to know who he is, and from where is he, but he separates from him before he gets to know that; and the third is a matter of the women. One of you approaches his wife and depletes his energy without fulfil her need’. So Abdullah Bin Amro Bin Al-Aas said, ‘So how is that, O Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘He should hold back and wait until that comes from both of them together’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And in another Hadeth, Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘From the most frustrating (of frustrations) is the frustration of a man who meets a man who is astounded about him, but he does not ask about his name, and his lineage, and his place (where he lives)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:28
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَوْماً لِجُلَسَائِهِ تَدْرُونَ مَا الْعَجْزُ قَالُوا اللَّهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ فَقَالَ الْعَجْزُ ثَلَاثَةٌ أَنْ يَبْدُرَ أَحَدُكُمْ بِطَعَامٍ يَصْنَعُهُ لِصَاحِبِهِ فَيُخْلِفَهُ وَ لَا يَأْتِيَهُ وَ الثَّانِيَةُ أَنْ يَصْحَبَ الرَّجُلُ مِنْكُمُ الرَّجُلَ أَوْ يُجَالِسَهُ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَعْلَمَ مَنْ هُوَ وَ مِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ فَيُفَارِقَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَعْلَمَ ذَلِكَ وَ الثَّالِثَةُ أَمْرُ النِّسَاءِ يَدْنُو أَحَدُكُمْ مِنْ أَهْلِهِ فَيَقْضِي حَاجَتَهُ وَ هِيَ لَمْ تَقْضِ حَاجَتَهَا فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ فَكَيْفَ ذَلِكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ يَتَحَوَّشُ وَ يَمْكُثُ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ ذَلِكَ مِنْهُمَا جَمِيعاً قَالَ وَ فِي حَدِيثٍ آخَرَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِنَّ مِنْ أَعْجَزِ الْعَجْزِ رَجُلًا لَقِيَ رَجُلًا فَأَعْجَبَهُ نَحْوُهُ فَلَمْ يَسْأَلْهُ عَنِ اسْمِهِ وَ نَسَبِهِ وَ مَوْضِعِهِ .

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And in another Hadeth, Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘From the most frustrating (of frustrations) is the frustration of a man who meets a man who is astounded about him, but he does not ask about his name, and his lineage, and his place (where he lives)’.

text: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Do not let the decency go away between you and your brother, preserve from it, for if it goes away, the bashfulness would go away’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:28
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ لَا تُذْهِبِ الْحِشْمَةَ بَيْنَكَ وَ بَيْنَ أَخِيكَ أَبْقِ مِنْهَا فَإِنَّ ذَهَابَهَا ذَهَابُ الْحَيَاءِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Do not let the decency go away between you and your brother, preserve from it, for if it goes away, the bashfulness would go away’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/579)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ismail, from Abdullah bin Wasil, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not trust in your brother with every trust, for a sudden abandonment would never be repairable’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:28
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَثِقْ بِأَخِيكَ كُلَّ الثِّقَةِ فَإِنَّ صِرْعَةَ الِاسْتِرْسَالِ لَنْ تُسْتَقَالَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ismail, from Abdullah bin Wasil, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not trust in your brother with every trust, for a sudden abandonment would never be repairable’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/579)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Moalla Bin Khunays, and Usman Bin Suleyman Al Nakhhas, from Mufazzal Bin Umar and Yunus Bin Zabyan who both said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Choose your brethren by two characteristics. So if these were both in them (fine), or else, turn away, then be distant, then be distant – preservation upon the Salat in its Prescribed timings, and the righteousness with the brethren in the (financial) difficulties and the affluence’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:28
citation.arabic_text: ا قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) اخْتَبِرُوا إِخْوَانَكُمْ بِخَصْلَتَيْنِ فَإِنْ كَانَتَا فِيهِمْ وَ إِلَّا فَاعْزُبْ ثُمَّ اعْزُبْ ثُمَّ اعْزُبْ مُحَافَظَةٍ عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ فِي مَوَاقِيتِهَا وَ الْبِرِّ بِالْإِخْوَانِ فِي الْعُسْرِ وَ الْيُسْرِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Moalla Bin Khunays, and Usman Bin Suleyman Al Nakhhas, from Mufazzal Bin Umar and Yunus Bin Zabyan who both said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Choose your brethren by two characteristics. So if these were both in them (fine), or else, turn away, then be distant, then be distant – preservation upon the Salat in its Prescribed timings, and the righteousness with the brethren in the (financial) difficulties and the affluence’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/580)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Amro Bin Abdul Aziz, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not leave (the saying of) ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful’, and even though after it is a poem’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:29
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَدَعْ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ بَعْدَهُ شِعْرٌ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Amro Bin Abdul Aziz, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not leave (the saying of) ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful’, and even though after it is a poem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/580)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Yusuf Bin Abdul Salam, from Sayf Bin Haroun a slave of the family of Ja’da who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Write ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful’ in the best of your writing, and do not extend the (letter) ‘Ba’ until you raise the (letter) ‘Seen’’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:29
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) اكْتُبْ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ مِنْ أَجْوَدِ كِتَابِكَ وَ لَا تَمُدَّ الْبَاءَ حَتَّى تَرْفَعَ السِّينَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Yusuf Bin Abdul Salam, from Sayf Bin Haroun a slave of the family of Ja’da who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Write ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful’ in the best of your writing, and do not extend the (letter) ‘Ba’ until you raise the (letter) ‘Seen’’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/580)

text: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Hassan Bin Al Sarry, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not write ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful’ to so and so, and there is no problem if you were to write upon the back of the letter to so and so’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:29
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لَا تَكْتُبْ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ لِفُلَانٍ وَ لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ تَكْتُبَ عَلَى ظَهْرِ الْكِتَابِ لِفُلَانٍ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Hassan Bin Al Sarry, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not write ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful’ to so and so, and there is no problem if you were to write upon the back of the letter to so and so’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/581)

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Nazar Bin Shuayb, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Hassan Bin Al Sarry, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not write inside the letter, ‘To the father of so and so’, and write to the father of so and so, and write upon the address, ‘To the father of so and so’’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:29
citation.arabic_text: لَا تَكْتُبْ دَاخِلَ الْكِتَابِ لِأَبِي فُلَانٍ وَ اكْتُبْ إِلَى أَبِي فُلَانٍ وَ اكْتُبْ عَلَى الْعُنْوَانِ لِأَبِي فُلَانٍ .
citation.translation: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Nazar Bin Shuayb, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Hassan Bin Al Sarry, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Do not write inside the letter, ‘To the father of so and so’, and write to the father of so and so, and write upon the address, ‘To the father of so and so’’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/581)

text: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who begins with the (name of the recipient) man in the letter. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it. That is from the preference that the man begins with (the name of) his brother to honour him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:29
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَبْدَأُ بِالرَّجُلِ فِي الْكِتَابِ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْفَضْلِ يَبْدَأُ الرَّجُلُ بِأَخِيهِ يُكْرِمُهُ .
citation.translation: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who begins with the (name of the recipient) man in the letter. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it. That is from the preference that the man begins with (the name of) his brother to honour him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/581)

text: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Al Ahmar, from Hadeed Bin Hakeym, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem with if the man were to begin by the name of his companions in the parchment before his own name’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:29
citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يَبْدَأَ الرَّجُلُ بِاسْمِ صَاحِبِهِ فِي الصَّحِيفَةِ قَبْلَ اسْمِهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Al Ahmar, from Hadeed Bin Hakeym, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem with if the man were to begin by the name of his companions in the parchment before his own name’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/581)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Murazam Bin Hakeem who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> ordered with a letter (to be written) regarding a need. So he wrote, then presented it to him<sup>asws</sup>, and there did not happen to be an exclusion clause (The expression, ‘If Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’) in it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How can you (people) be hoping for the completion of this (matter), and there is no exclusion clause (The expression, ‘If Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’) in it. Look at every place where there does not happen to be an exclusion clause, so (insert) the exclusion clause in it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:29
citation.arabic_text: أَمَرَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) بِكِتَابٍ فِي حَاجَةٍ فَكُتِبَ ثُمَّ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ اسْتِثْنَاءٌ فَقَالَ كَيْفَ رَجَوْتُمْ أَنْ يَتِمَّ هَذَا وَ لَيْسَ فِيهِ اسْتِثْنَاءٌ انْظُرُوا كُلَّ مَوْضِعٍ لَا يَكُونُ فِيهِ اسْتِثْنَاءٌ فَاسْتَثْنُوا فِيهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Murazam Bin Hakeem who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> ordered with a letter (to be written) regarding a need. So he wrote, then presented it to him<sup>asws</sup>, and there did not happen to be an exclusion clause (The expression, ‘If Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’) in it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How can you (people) be hoping for the completion of this (matter), and there is no exclusion clause (The expression, ‘If Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’) in it. Look at every place where there does not happen to be an exclusion clause, so (insert) the exclusion clause in it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/581)

text: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> would (sprinkle) dust upon the letter (to dry the ink), and said: ‘There is no problem with it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:29
citation.arabic_text: لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> would (sprinkle) dust upon the letter (to dry the ink), and said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (2/581)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, (It has been narrated) from Ali Bin Atiyya that he saw a letter of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (sprinkled) with dust (to dry the ink)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:29
citation.arabic_text: مُتَرَّبَةً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, (It has been narrated) from Ali Bin Atiyya that he saw a letter of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (sprinkled) with dust (to dry the ink)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/582)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Abdul Malik Bin Utba, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the papers which tend to accumulate. ‘Can they be burned with the fire and therein is something from the Mention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No! You should wash it out with the water first, before (burning)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:30
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْقَرَاطِيسِ تَجْتَمِعُ هَلْ تُحْرَقُ بِالنَّارِ وَ فِيهَا شَيْ‏ءٌ مِنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ قَالَ لَا تُغْسَلُ بِالْمَاءِ أَوَّلًا قَبْلُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Abdul Malik Bin Utba, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the papers which tend to accumulate. ‘Can they be burned with the fire and therein is something from the Mention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No! You should wash it out with the water first, before (burning)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (12/582)

text: From him, from Al Washha, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Do not burn the papers, but delete these and (then) burn them’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:30
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ لَا تُحْرِقُوا الْقَرَاطِيسَ وَ لَكِنِ امْحُوهَا وَ حَرِّقُوهَا .
citation.translation: From him, from Al Washha, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Do not burn the papers, but delete these and (then) burn them’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Zurara who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the Name from the Names of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the man deletes it with the saliva. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Delete it with the cleanest of what you can find (water)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:30
citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الِاسْمِ مِنْ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ يَمْحُوهُ الرَّجُلُ بِالتُّفْلِ قَالَ امْحُوهُ بِأَطْهَرِ مَا تَجِدُونَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Zurara who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the Name from the Names of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the man deletes it with the saliva. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Delete it with the cleanest of what you can find (water)’.

text: Ali, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘(You can) delete the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted and His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention with the cleanest of what you can find’, and he<sup>saww</sup> forbade to burn the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and forbade from deleting with the pens’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:30
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) امْحُوا كِتَابَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَ ذِكْرَهُ بِأَطْهَرِ مَا تَجِدُونَ وَ نَهَى أَنْ يُحْرَقَ كِتَابُ اللَّهِ وَ نَهَى أَنْ يُمْحَى بِالْأَقْلَامِ .
citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘(You can) delete the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted and His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention with the cleanest of what you can find’, and he<sup>saww</sup> forbade to burn the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and forbade from deleting with the pens’.

text: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> regarding the surfaces in which there is Mention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Wash it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF SOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS (al-Kafi, vol 2), 4:30
citation.arabic_text: الظُّهُورِ الَّتِي فِيهَا ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ قَالَ اغْسِلْهَا .
citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> regarding the surfaces in which there is Mention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Wash it’.
